# Working Draft

This document is the on-disk workspace for the model-consensus architecture pass. It intentionally starts as a target-architecture shell, not as a preservation plan for the current implementation.

The final version should answer one question:

```text
What architecture makes Codex Dock fast, stable, resilient, provider-agnostic, and simple on the client?
```

# Raw Goal

Design the perfect architecture for Codex Dock where the relay does the hard work and the client receives a clean, simple, robust protocol. The architecture should support full updates, incremental updates, resync, transient failure tolerance, fast startup, provider abstraction, and future non-Codex providers such as Claude Code without requiring client rewrites.

Do not implement anything in this pass.

# Non-Negotiables

- The relay is the aggregator and durability boundary for Dock state.
- The client does not decode raw Codex app-server details.
- The client does not stitch together history, live state, cursors, and failure recovery.
- The client can render from one clean over-the-wire model.
- The relay supports full snapshot, incremental updates, and explicit resync.
- Slow or failing upstream providers never erase last-known-good client state.
- Runtime/provider weirdness is isolated behind relay-side adapters.
- Secrets stay relay-side.
- The design does not preserve current architecture for its own sake.

1	---
2	title: "Codex Dock - Home Refresh and Not Loaded Root Cause"
3	date: 2026-05-29
4	status: investigation
5	owners: [Amir]
6	doc_type: root_cause_analysis
7	source_repo_head: 3ed11ad
8	scope: investigation_only_no_source_fixes
9	related:
10	  - docs/CODEX_DOCK_SINGLE_ENDPOINT_PER_HOST_GOALS_2026-05-29.md
11	  - CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift
12	  - CodexDock/State/AppServerDockClient.swift
13	  - CodexDock/State/DockSessionProjection.swift
14	  - CodexDock/State/SessionRowProjector.swift
15	  - scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs
16	  - scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs
17	  - /Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/README.md
18	  - /Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs
19	  - /Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs
20	---
21	
22	# TL;DR
23	
24	There are two separate problems that look like one bad UI state.
25	
26	1. The Home row count flaps because the client rebuilds each refresh from only the hosts that have completed in that refresh. Amir-M5 finishes quickly, so its rows stay visible. Home is slower, so when Home is selected, the current refresh temporarily has zero Home rows and a `Checking` host state until Home's new request finishes.
27	
28	2. `Not loaded` is coming from the upstream app-server data. Codex app-server intentionally returns `status: { "type": "notLoaded" }` for stored history rows that are not currently loaded in memory. The relay currently does not merge live status into `thread/list` rows; it only attaches a `liveOverlay`. So the app is not inventing `Not loaded`, but it is presenting an upstream implementation detail too loudly.
29	
30	Home is synced to the same client repo commit as this Mac, `3ed11ad`. The current Home relay is reachable and healthy. The old code and old Home checkout were confounders earlier, but they are not the whole explanation for the current UI behavior.
31	
32	# Investigation Bounds
33	
34	This pass did not make source-code changes. It used direct JSON-RPC relay probes, simulator unified logs, repo source reads, and Codex app-server source reads.
35	
36	No screenshots were used. No simulator UI automation was used. This avoids stealing macOS focus while still proving the timing and data path.
37	
38	Current code version:
39	
40	- Local repo: `codex-dock-agents-tab-live-counts`
41	- Local HEAD: `3ed11ad Bound active Dock session paging`
42	- Local worktree before writing this doc: clean
43	- Home repo HEAD: `3ed11ad`
44	- Home worktree status from `git status --short --untracked-files=all`: clean output
45	
46	# User-Visible Symptom
47	
48	When the Dock view is filtered or focused on Home, it can show this loop:
49	
50	```text
51	Home: 200 sessions
52	Home: Checking
53	Home: 0 shown
54	Home: 200 sessions
55	```
56	
57	Amir-M5 usually looks stable because it finishes first. If the selected host is Amir-M5, the partial snapshot already contains Amir-M5 rows, so there is no visible drop to zero for that selected host.
58	
59	# Ground Truth Summary
60	
61	## Current relay health
62	
63	Both relays were online at the time of the direct probe.
64	
65	```text
66	Amir-M5 statusz:
67	  httpStatus: 200
68	  ok: true
69	  host.id: Amir-M5
70	  history.lastHealth.status: up
71	  liveStatus.overlayState: ready
72	  liveStatus.endpoints: 2
73	  liveStatus.rows: 10
74	  history pool pending: 0
75	
76	Home statusz:
77	  httpStatus: 200
78	  ok: true
79	  host.id: home
80	  history.lastHealth.status: up
81	  liveStatus.overlayState: ready
82	  liveStatus.endpoints: 0
83	  liveStatus.rows: 0
84	  history pool pending: 3
85	```
86	
87	Home's `lastClientFacingError` at the time of the probe was:
88	
89	```text
90	at: 2026-05-29T19:16:08.886Z
91	subsystem: history
92	method: thread/list
93	code: ECONNREFUSED
94	retryable: true
95	message: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4500
96	```
97	
98	That error lines up with the earlier service restart. The current probe after that error succeeded.
99	
100	## Current list-call timing and status distribution
101	
102	Direct JSON-RPC probe at `2026-05-29T19:30:36.358Z`:
103	
104	```text
105	Amir-M5 activeHuman:
106	  durationMs: 484
107	  rows: 100
108	  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
109	  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=2, rows=10
110	  nextCursorPresent: true
111	
112	Amir-M5 activeAgents:
113	  durationMs: 159
114	  rows: 100
115	  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
116	  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=2, rows=10
117	  nextCursorPresent: true
118	
119	Home activeHuman:
120	  durationMs: 5978
121	  rows: 100
122	  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
123	  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=0, rows=0
124	  nextCursorPresent: true
125	
126	Home activeAgents:
127	  durationMs: 3769
128	  rows: 100
129	  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
130	  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=0, rows=0
131	  nextCursorPresent: true
132	```
133	
134	Important read:
135	
136	- Current app behavior loads one page per active scope.
137	- One page is observed as 100 rows from app-server even though the client asks for `limit: 250`.
138	- The Dock runs two active scopes per host: human and agents.
139	- With two hosts, current successful refreshes therefore produce `400` rows:
140	  - Amir-M5 human: 100
141	  - Amir-M5 agents: 100
142	  - Home human: 100
143	  - Home agents: 100
144	
145	## Home is slower enough to expose the client bug
146	
147	At this probe, Home's slowest scope took `5978ms`. Amir-M5's slowest scope took `484ms`.
148	
149	The client publishes a partial snapshot as soon as the first host finishes. That means the UI can enter a partial state after Amir-M5 finishes, while Home is still loading. In that partial snapshot, Home has a host state of `Checking` and no rows.
150	
151	## Amir-M5 proves the relay has live knowledge but does not merge it into list rows
152	
153	Amir-M5 had `10` live loaded rows according to `thread/loaded/list`.
154	
155	Two of those live row IDs also appeared in the first `thread/list` page, but their list statuses were still `notLoaded`:
156	
157	```json
158	{
159	  "loadedRows": 10,
160	  "listRows": 100,
161	  "overlapRows": 2,
162	  "overlaps": [
163	    {
164	      "id": "019e7376-aa6f-7171-85b5-5e63cffb0158",
165	      "status": "notLoaded",
166	      "source": "vscode"
167	    },
168	    {
169	      "id": "019e7456-af5f-7561-9cb2-0db296c62b49",
170	      "status": "notLoaded",
171	      "source": "vscode"
172	    }
173	  ]
174	}
175	```
176	
177	That is the clearest proof that the relay/app-server combination currently does not make `thread/list` a good live-status source.
178	
179	# Simulator Evidence
180	
181	The simulator used was the booted `iPhone 17`:
182	
183	```text
184	BAD95C8E-3E57-4818-9B90-E4ED22593B4B
185	```
186	
187	The simulator logs show this repeated shape:
188	
189	```text
190	2026-05-29 14:20:51.857 dock reload started hosts=2 show_loading=true
191	2026-05-29 14:20:52.543 connectivity overall status=Partial message=Online 1/2, checking 1
192	2026-05-29 14:20:58.047 connectivity overall status=Online message=2 hosts online
193	2026-05-29 14:20:58.047 dock reload finished hosts=2 rows=400 duration_ms=6190
194	
195	2026-05-29 14:21:03.052 dock reload started hosts=2 show_loading=false
196	2026-05-29 14:21:03.606 connectivity overall status=Partial message=Online 1/2, checking 1
197	2026-05-29 14:21:07.661 connectivity overall status=Online message=2 hosts online
198	2026-05-29 14:21:07.661 dock reload finished hosts=2 rows=400 duration_ms=4606
199	
200	2026-05-29 14:29:25.424 dock reload started hosts=2 show_loading=false
201	2026-05-29 14:29:25.988 connectivity overall status=Partial message=Online 1/2, checking 1
202	2026-05-29 14:29:31.071 connectivity overall status=Online message=2 hosts online
203	2026-05-29 14:29:31.071 dock reload finished hosts=2 rows=400 duration_ms=5647
204	
205	2026-05-29 14:30:27.324 dock reload started hosts=2 show_loading=false
206	2026-05-29 14:30:27.872 connectivity overall status=Partial message=Online 1/2, checking 1
207	2026-05-29 14:30:33.280 connectivity overall status=Online message=2 hosts online
208	2026-05-29 14:30:33.280 dock reload finished hosts=2 rows=400 duration_ms=5956
209	```
210	
211	This proves:
212	
213	- The app is not staying permanently offline.
214	- The app is not losing the relay connection.
215	- The app is repeatedly entering a partial snapshot during normal refresh.
216	- The partial window often lasts around 3.5 to 6.9 seconds.
217	- The refresh loop then waits 5 seconds after the refresh completes before starting another refresh.
218	
219	So the problem is not overlapping refreshes. It is destructive partial refresh state.
220	
221	# Client Code Path
222	
223	## Refresh loop
224	
225	`CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`:
226	
227	- `runDockRefreshLoop()` performs the first `await dockStore.load()`.
228	- Then it sleeps for `DockStore.defaultAutoRefreshInterval`.
229	- Then it performs `await dockStore.refresh()`.
230	- Because it awaits `refresh()`, refreshes are not intentionally concurrent.
231	
232	`CodexDock/Configuration/CodexDockConstants.swift`:
233	
234	```swift
235	public static let autoRefreshInterval: Duration = .seconds(5)
236	```
237	
238	Plain meaning: the app waits for a refresh to finish, waits 5 more seconds, then starts the next refresh.
239	
240	## Partial host load
241	
242	`CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift` is the main cause of the Home zero-row flicker.
243	
244	The load starts with a fresh empty outcome list:
245	
246	```swift
247	var outcomes: [HostLoadOutcome] = []
248	var checkingHostIDs = Set(hosts.map(\.id))
249	```
250	
251	As each host completes:
252	
253	```swift
254	outcomes.append(outcome)
255	checkingHostIDs.remove(outcome.host.id)
256	...
257	if !checkingHostIDs.isEmpty {
258	    state = .loaded(makeSnapshot(results: outcomes, checkingHostIDs: checkingHostIDs))
259	}
260	```
261	
262	`makeSnapshot(...)` then builds rows only from the current refresh outcomes:
263	
264	```swift
265	var summaries: [SessionSummary] = []
266	...
267	for outcome in results {
268	    ...
269	    summaries.append(contentsOf: hostDedupedSummaries)
270	}
271	...
272	for host in hosts where checkingHostIDs.contains(host.id) {
273	    hostStatesByID[host.id] = DockHostStateViewModel(host: hostViewModel, status: .checking)
274	}
275	...
276	let rows = projector.rows(from: summaries)
277	```
278	
279	The missing piece: there is no "last good rows per host" cache used for a still-checking host. A still-checking host contributes host state only, not stale rows.
280	
281	## Why Home selected goes to zero
282	
283	`CodexDock/State/DockSessionProjection.swift` filters visible rows by selected host:
284	
285	```swift
286	if !options.filters.selectedHostIDs.isEmpty,
287	   !options.filters.selectedHostIDs.contains(row.id.hostID) {
288	    return false
289	}
290	```
291	
292	During a partial refresh:
293	
294	- Amir-M5 rows are in `snapshot.rows`.
295	- Home is only in `snapshot.hostStates` as `.checking`.
296	- Home rows from the previous successful refresh are not carried forward.
297	- If the selected host filter is Home, the visible row list is empty.
298	
299	That exactly matches the observed `Home -> 0 -> Checking -> 200` behavior.
300	
301	## Current paging improvement
302	
303	At `3ed11ad`, active session paging is bounded:
304	
305	```swift
306	public static let activeSessionMaxPages = 1
307	```
308	
309	`DockSessionQuery.activeHuman` and `DockSessionQuery.activeAgents` both use that `maxPages`.
310	
311	`AppServerDockClient.loadSessions(...)` stops after `maxPages`:
312	
313	```swift
314	if let maxPages = query.maxPages, pageCount >= maxPages {
315	    cursor = nil
316	    break
317	}
318	```
319	
320	This prevents the older active-Dock behavior where the app drained every active cursor from Home before finishing. Earlier in this same work session, an app-shaped full cursor drain against Home showed:
321	
322	```text
323	Home human all-pages:
324	  10 pages
325	  958 rows
326	  19324ms
327	
328	Home agents all-pages:
329	  reached page 13
330	  1300 rows
331	  66601ms
332	  then timed out at 90s before completion
333	```
334	
335	That explains why the pre-`3ed11ad` experience was much worse. It does not fully solve the current UI problem because the current one-page Home request can still take about 4 to 6 seconds, and stale Home rows are still dropped while the new Home request is in flight.
336	
337	# Relay Code Path
338	
339	## `thread/list` mostly passes through history rows
340	
341	`scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`:
342	
343	```js
344	async function aggregateThreadList(config, params = {}) {
345	  const historyParams = clampThreadListParams(params);
346	  const history = await readHistoryThreadList(config, historyParams);
347	  const data = Array.isArray(history.data) ? history.data : [];
348	  const summaryCache = threadSummaryCacheForConfig(config);
349	  const dataWithSummaries = summaryCache.decorateRows(data);
350	  summaryCache.warmRows(data);
351	  const liveOverlay = history.liveOverlay || liveStatusCacheForConfig(config).liveOverlay();
352	  return {
353	    ...history,
354	    data: dataWithSummaries,
355	    liveOverlay,
356	  };
357	}
358	```
359	
360	What this means:
361	
362	- The relay asks the raw history app-server for `thread/list`.
363	- It decorates row summaries.
364	- It warms summaries in the background.
365	- It attaches `liveOverlay`.
366	- It does not replace row status with live status.
367	- It does not insert loaded live rows into the list.
368	- It does not keep a cached stable host snapshot for the client.
369	
370	## Live discovery is separate
371	
372	`scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` discovers live loopback app-server processes:
373	
374	```js
375	const endpoints = discoverLoopbackEndpoints()
376	  .filter((endpoint) => !excludedURLs.has(canonicalURLString(endpoint.url)));
377	```
378	
379	It then calls:
380	
381	```js
382	thread/loaded/list
383	thread/read
384	```
385	
386	against those live endpoints and builds a live status cache.
387	
388	The important Home result was:
389	
390	```text
391	Home liveStatus.endpoints: 0
392	Home liveStatus.rows: 0
393	```
394	
395	The important Amir-M5 result was:
396	
397	```text
398	Amir-M5 liveStatus.endpoints: 2
399	Amir-M5 liveStatus.rows: 10
400	```
401	
402	If Home is expected to have live Codex sessions, the next investigation should ask why the relay sees zero non-history loopback app-server processes on Home. The relay's discovery regex only sees process lines shaped like:
403	
404	```text
405	codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:<port>
406	```
407	
408	If Home's active sessions are launched under a different command shape, different user, container, service manager, or socket shape, this discovery path will miss them.
409	
410	## Current relay tests protect "do not merge live status into list"
411	
412	`scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` has a test named:
413	
414	```text
415	relay thread/list keeps history status while focused detail can still route live
416	```
417	
418	The test sets up:
419	
420	- live row status: `active`
421	- history row status: `notLoaded`
422	
423	Then it asserts the list row still says:
424	
425	```js
426	assert.equal(rows[0].status.type, "notLoaded");
427	```
428	
429	Plain meaning: the relay behavior that makes the Dock list mostly `Not loaded` is not accidental in the current codebase. It is an intentional contract today. The relay can route detail calls to the live owner, but the list remains history-first.
430	
431	# Raw Codex App-Server Code Path
432	
433	The upstream Codex app-server source confirms that `notLoaded` is a real state with a narrow meaning.
434	
435	`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/README.md`:
436	
437	```text
438	thread/list ... Each returned thread includes status (ThreadStatus), defaulting to notLoaded when the thread is not currently loaded.
439	```
440	
441	The same README says:
442	
443	```text
444	thread/loaded/list - list the thread ids currently loaded in memory.
445	```
446	
447	`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs`:
448	
449	```rust
450	status: ThreadStatus::NotLoaded,
451	```
452	
453	is the default status assigned when a stored thread is converted into a `Thread`.
454	
455	Then `thread/list` asks the thread watch manager for loaded statuses:
456	
457	```rust
458	let statuses = self
459	    .thread_watch_manager
460	    .loaded_statuses_for_threads(status_ids)
461	    .await;
462	...
463	if let Some(status) = statuses.get(&thread.id) {
464	    thread.status = status.clone();
465	}
466	```
467	
468	`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs`:
469	
470	```rust
471	fn loaded_status_for_thread(&self, thread_id: &str) -> ThreadStatus {
472	    self.status_for(thread_id)
473	        .unwrap_or(ThreadStatus::NotLoaded)
474	}
475	```
476	
477	and:
478	
479	```rust
480	fn loaded_thread_status(runtime: &RuntimeFacts) -> ThreadStatus {
481	    if !runtime.is_loaded {
482	        return ThreadStatus::NotLoaded;
483	    }
484	    ...
485	}
486	```
487	
488	Plain meaning: upstream `notLoaded` does not mean "this row is missing basic list data." It means "this thread is not currently loaded in this app-server process's runtime memory."
489	
490	# Root Cause
491	
492	## Root cause 1: destructive partial snapshots
493	
494	The Home zero-row behavior is a client state-management bug.
495	
496	The Dock should treat a refresh as "new data is being fetched for a host." Instead, it treats a still-checking host as "this host currently contributes no rows." That is why a Home filter can collapse to zero even though the app had good Home rows from the previous refresh.
497	
498	This is exposed by Home because Home is slower. Amir-M5 is fast enough that its partial period is tiny from the user's point of view.
499	
500	## Root cause 2: `Not loaded` is technically true but product-hostile as a primary row badge
501	
502	The upstream meaning is precise: the thread exists in history, but it is not currently loaded in a runtime owner.
503	
504	For Dock, that status is not very useful as the dominant row state because most history rows will naturally be `notLoaded`. The row still has useful data:
505	
506	- title or preview
507	- cwd/repository
508	- branch
509	- last activity
510	- source type
511	- host
512	
513	So the row is not "not loaded" in the way a user reads that phrase. It is only "runtime status not loaded."
514	
515	## Root cause 3: the relay leaves too much list assembly burden on the client
516	
517	The relay currently gives the client:
518	
519	- history pages from `thread/list`
520	- a separate `liveOverlay`
521	- live routing for detail operations
522	
523	It does not give the client:
524	
525	- a stable per-host Dock snapshot
526	- a stale-while-refresh contract
527	- merged live statuses for list rows
528	- a server-side answer to "show me the current Dock list for this host"
529	
530	So the client is forced to fan out and rebuild the Dock view from lower-level pieces. That is workable for a fast single host. It is brittle when one host is slower and the UI needs stable filtered views.
531	
532	## Root cause 4: Home has no discovered live rows
533	
534	Home's live status cache reported:
535	
536	```text
537	endpoints: 0
538	rows: 0
539	```
540	
541	That means Home cannot currently upgrade list status from live app-server owners through the relay's live discovery path. This may be expected if Home has no live Codex sessions. If Home does have live sessions, this is a separate relay discovery problem.
542	
543	# What Is Not The Root Cause
544	
545	## Not raw connectivity
546	
547	Both relays responded to `/statusz`. Both relays served `thread/list`. Simulator logs repeatedly recovered to:
548	
549	```text
550	Online message=2 hosts online
551	```
552	
553	## Not overlapping refreshes
554	
555	The refresh loop awaits each refresh, then sleeps 5 seconds. There is no evidence that the app is starting a new Dock refresh before the previous one completes in normal foreground operation.
556	
557	## Not a Swift string-only bug
558	
559	The Swift mapper maps upstream `notLoaded` to the Dock row status:
560	
561	```swift
562	case .notLoaded:
563	    return .notLoaded
564	```
565	
566	The row projector then displays:
567	
568	```swift
569	case .notLoaded:
570	    return .notLoaded
571	```
572	
573	The label is confusing, but the data starts upstream.
574	
575	## Not only the old Home checkout
576	
577	Earlier, Home was running old code and that was a real confounder. Current evidence after syncing Home to `3ed11ad` still shows:
578	
579	- Home requests are much slower than Amir-M5.
580	- Home rows disappear during partial refresh.
581	- all current list rows return `notLoaded`.
582	
583	# UX Meaning
584	
585	The UI should distinguish these concepts:
586	
587	```text
588	Host reachability:
589	  Is the host online?
590	
591	Host refresh state:
592	  Are we refreshing this host right now?
593	
594	Row runtime status:
595	  Is this thread currently loaded/running/idle in a live app-server?
596	
597	Row list availability:
598	  Do we have enough data to show the row in the Dock list?
599	```
600	
601	Today those concepts are collapsed in the user's experience:
602	
603	- A refreshing host looks like it temporarily has no rows.
604	- A history row whose runtime owner is not loaded looks like the row itself is "not loaded."
605	- A slow host looks unstable even when it is online.
606	
607	# Candidate Fixes For Discussion Only
608	
609	No fix was applied in this investigation pass.
610	
611	## Option A: client stale-while-refresh per host
612	
613	Keep each host's last successful rows while a new refresh for that host is in flight.
614	
615	During refresh:
616	
617	```text
618	Home: 200 sessions, refreshing
619	Rows: still visible from last successful Home snapshot
620	```
621	
622	When Home finishes:
623	
624	```text
625	Home: 200 sessions
626	Rows: replaced with fresh Home rows
627	```
628	
629	This directly fixes the zero-row flicker. It is probably the smallest product-correct fix for the current symptom.
630	
631	Primary simulator test requirement:
632	
633	- Configure two hosts.
634	- Make one host slow enough to finish after the other.
635	- Select/filter the slow host after an initial successful load.
636	- Trigger refresh.
637	- Verify the slow host keeps its previous rows while its host state indicates refresh/checking.
638	
639	If current simulator hooks cannot force a slow host, add hooks. This should not rely on unit tests as the primary proof.
640	
641	## Option B: split `checking` from `refreshing`
642	
643	Use `checking` for first load or unknown host state only.
644	
645	Use `refreshing` when the host already has a last-good snapshot.
646	
647	This makes the UI language match reality:
648	
649	```text
650	First load:
651	  Home: Checking
652	  Rows: none yet
653	
654	Later refresh:
655	  Home: Refreshing
656	  Rows: retained
657	```
658	
659	This is strongly related to Option A and may be part of the same client fix.
660	
661	## Option C: relay-level Dock snapshot endpoint
662	
663	Add a relay-owned endpoint shaped for the Dock, for example:
664	
665	```text
666	dock/snapshot
667	```
668	
669	The relay would own:
670	
671	- history paging policy
672	- status merge policy
673	- stale-while-refresh behavior
674	- per-host caching
675	- live status integration
676	
677	The client would ask for the current host snapshot instead of rebuilding everything from lower-level history and live endpoints.
678	
679	This is a bigger architectural fix, but it fits the product direction better if the relay is meant to simplify the phone client.
680	
681	Primary simulator test requirement:
682	
683	- App connected to real relay.
684	- Relay snapshot refresh in progress.
685	- Host-filtered UI remains stable.
686	- Offline/error states still render correctly when the host path is unavailable.
687	
688	## Option D: relay merges live status into `thread/list` rows
689	
690	The relay already knows about live rows on Amir-M5. It could replace `notLoaded` status on matching list rows when a live row exists.
691	
692	This would change an existing protected behavior. `scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` currently asserts that history status wins for `thread/list`, even when live detail routing is available.
693	
694	So this is not a trivial cleanup. It is a product/API contract decision.
695	
696	## Option E: reduce `Not loaded` prominence
697	
698	Even if upstream keeps `notLoaded`, the Dock row badge does not have to present it as the main row status.
699	
700	Possible UX interpretations:
701	
702	- Show no status badge for `notLoaded` history rows.
703	- Show `History` instead of `Not loaded`.
704	- Show runtime statuses only when they are meaningful: `Running`, `Needs input`, `Error`, maybe `Idle`.
705	- Move `Not loaded` into a debug/detail field or filter, not the default row badge.
706	
707	This does not fix the Home zero-row flicker, but it addresses the "everything says Not loaded" product problem.
708	
709	## Option F: investigate Home live discovery
710	
711	If Home is expected to have active Codex sessions, inspect why the relay sees:
712	
713	```text
714	liveStatus.endpoints: 0
715	liveStatus.rows: 0
716	```
717	
718	The likely checks:
719	
720	```bash
721	ps -axo pid,command | rg 'codex app-server --listen ws://127\\.0\\.0\\.1:'
722	```
723	
724	and whether Home sessions are launched:
725	
726	- under the same user as the relay
727	- with a different command shape
728	- in a container namespace
729	- through a non-loopback socket
730	- without `codex app-server --listen ...`
731	
732	This is separate from the client stale-row bug. Fixing live discovery would make statuses more useful, but it would not by itself stop stale Home rows from disappearing during refresh.
733	
734	# Recommended Direction
735	
736	The clean product path is probably:
737	
738	1. Fix the client to retain last-good host rows during refresh.
739	2. Rename the refresh state so first load is `Checking` and later refresh is visibly different.
740	3. Decide whether `Not loaded` should remain a visible row status at all.
741	4. Separately decide whether the relay should provide a Dock-shaped snapshot or merge live statuses into list rows.
742	5. Investigate Home live discovery only if Home should have active live sessions right now.
743	
744	The first fix should be simulator-proven. A unit test can cover the state reducer behavior, but it should not be treated as completion evidence. The important proof is the visible simulator behavior with a slow host selected.
745	
746	# Commands Used
747

---
title: "Codex Dock - Home Refresh and Not Loaded Root Cause"
date: 2026-05-29
status: investigation
owners: [Amir]
doc_type: root_cause_analysis
source_repo_head: 3ed11ad
scope: investigation_only_no_source_fixes
related:
  - docs/CODEX_DOCK_SINGLE_ENDPOINT_PER_HOST_GOALS_2026-05-29.md
  - CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift
  - CodexDock/State/AppServerDockClient.swift
  - CodexDock/State/DockSessionProjection.swift
  - CodexDock/State/SessionRowProjector.swift
  - scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs
  - scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs
  - /Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/README.md
  - /Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs
  - /Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs
---

# TL;DR

There are two separate problems that look like one bad UI state.

1. The Home row count flaps because the client rebuilds each refresh from only the hosts that have completed in that refresh. Amir-M5 finishes quickly, so its rows stay visible. Home is slower, so when Home is selected, the current refresh temporarily has zero Home rows and a `Checking` host state until Home's new request finishes.

2. `Not loaded` is coming from the upstream app-server data. Codex app-server intentionally returns `status: { "type": "notLoaded" }` for stored history rows that are not currently loaded in memory. The relay currently does not merge live status into `thread/list` rows; it only attaches a `liveOverlay`. So the app is not inventing `Not loaded`, but it is presenting an upstream implementation detail too loudly.

Home is synced to the same client repo commit as this Mac, `3ed11ad`. The current Home relay is reachable and healthy. The old code and old Home checkout were confounders earlier, but they are not the whole explanation for the current UI behavior.

# Investigation Bounds

This pass did not make source-code changes. It used direct JSON-RPC relay probes, simulator unified logs, repo source reads, and Codex app-server source reads.

No screenshots were used. No simulator UI automation was used. This avoids stealing macOS focus while still proving the timing and data path.

Current code version:

- Local repo: `codex-dock-agents-tab-live-counts`
- Local HEAD: `3ed11ad Bound active Dock session paging`
- Local worktree before writing this doc: clean
- Home repo HEAD: `3ed11ad`
- Home worktree status from `git status --short --untracked-files=all`: clean output

# User-Visible Symptom

When the Dock view is filtered or focused on Home, it can show this loop:

```text
Home: 200 sessions
Home: Checking
Home: 0 shown
Home: 200 sessions
```

Amir-M5 usually looks stable because it finishes first. If the selected host is Amir-M5, the partial snapshot already contains Amir-M5 rows, so there is no visible drop to zero for that selected host.

# Ground Truth Summary

## Current relay health

Both relays were online at the time of the direct probe.

```text
Amir-M5 statusz:
  httpStatus: 200
  ok: true
  host.id: Amir-M5
  history.lastHealth.status: up
  liveStatus.overlayState: ready
  liveStatus.endpoints: 2
  liveStatus.rows: 10
  history pool pending: 0

Home statusz:
  httpStatus: 200
  ok: true
  host.id: home
  history.lastHealth.status: up
  liveStatus.overlayState: ready
  liveStatus.endpoints: 0
  liveStatus.rows: 0
  history pool pending: 3
```

Home's `lastClientFacingError` at the time of the probe was:

```text
at: 2026-05-29T19:16:08.886Z
subsystem: history
method: thread/list
code: ECONNREFUSED
retryable: true
message: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4500
```

That error lines up with the earlier service restart. The current probe after that error succeeded.

## Current list-call timing and status distribution

Direct JSON-RPC probe at `2026-05-29T19:30:36.358Z`:

```text
Amir-M5 activeHuman:
  durationMs: 484
  rows: 100
  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=2, rows=10
  nextCursorPresent: true

Amir-M5 activeAgents:
  durationMs: 159
  rows: 100
  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=2, rows=10
  nextCursorPresent: true

Home activeHuman:
  durationMs: 5978
  rows: 100
  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=0, rows=0
  nextCursorPresent: true

Home activeAgents:
  durationMs: 3769
  rows: 100
  statusTypes: { notLoaded: 100 }
  liveOverlay: ready, endpoints=0, rows=0
  nextCursorPresent: true
```

Important read:

- Current app behavior loads one page per active scope.
- One page is observed as 100 rows from app-server even though the client asks for `limit: 250`.
- The Dock runs two active scopes per host: human and agents.
- With two hosts, current successful refreshes therefore produce `400` rows:
  - Amir-M5 human: 100
  - Amir-M5 agents: 100
  - Home human: 100
  - Home agents: 100

## Home is slower enough to expose the client bug

At this probe, Home's slowest scope took `5978ms`. Amir-M5's slowest scope took `484ms`.

The client publishes a partial snapshot as soon as the first host finishes. That means the UI can enter a partial state after Amir-M5 finishes, while Home is still loading. In that partial snapshot, Home has a host state of `Checking` and no rows.

## Amir-M5 proves the relay has live knowledge but does not merge it into list rows

Amir-M5 had `10` live loaded rows according to `thread/loaded/list`.

Two of those live row IDs also appeared in the first `thread/list` page, but their list statuses were still `notLoaded`:

```json
{
  "loadedRows": 10,
  "listRows": 100,
  "overlapRows": 2,
  "overlaps": [
    {
      "id": "019e7376-aa6f-7171-85b5-5e63cffb0158",
      "status": "notLoaded",
      "source": "vscode"
    },
    {
      "id": "019e7456-af5f-7561-9cb2-0db296c62b49",
      "status": "notLoaded",
      "source": "vscode"
    }
  ]
}
```

That is the clearest proof that the relay/app-server combination currently does not make `thread/list` a good live-status source.

# Simulator Evidence

The simulator used was the booted `iPhone 17`:


# Client Code Path

## Refresh loop

`CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`:

- `runDockRefreshLoop()` performs the first `await dockStore.load()`.
- Then it sleeps for `DockStore.defaultAutoRefreshInterval`.
- Then it performs `await dockStore.refresh()`.
- Because it awaits `refresh()`, refreshes are not intentionally concurrent.

`CodexDock/Configuration/CodexDockConstants.swift`:

```swift
public static let autoRefreshInterval: Duration = .seconds(5)
```

Plain meaning: the app waits for a refresh to finish, waits 5 more seconds, then starts the next refresh.

## Partial host load

`CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift` is the main cause of the Home zero-row flicker.

The load starts with a fresh empty outcome list:

```swift
var outcomes: [HostLoadOutcome] = []
var checkingHostIDs = Set(hosts.map(\.id))
```

As each host completes:

```swift
outcomes.append(outcome)
checkingHostIDs.remove(outcome.host.id)
...
if !checkingHostIDs.isEmpty {
    state = .loaded(makeSnapshot(results: outcomes, checkingHostIDs: checkingHostIDs))
}
```

`makeSnapshot(...)` then builds rows only from the current refresh outcomes:

```swift
var summaries: [SessionSummary] = []
...
for outcome in results {
    ...
    summaries.append(contentsOf: hostDedupedSummaries)
}
...
for host in hosts where checkingHostIDs.contains(host.id) {
    hostStatesByID[host.id] = DockHostStateViewModel(host: hostViewModel, status: .checking)
}
...
let rows = projector.rows(from: summaries)
```

The missing piece: there is no "last good rows per host" cache used for a still-checking host. A still-checking host contributes host state only, not stale rows.

## Why Home selected goes to zero

`CodexDock/State/DockSessionProjection.swift` filters visible rows by selected host:

```swift
if !options.filters.selectedHostIDs.isEmpty,
   !options.filters.selectedHostIDs.contains(row.id.hostID) {
    return false
}
```

During a partial refresh:

- Amir-M5 rows are in `snapshot.rows`.
- Home is only in `snapshot.hostStates` as `.checking`.
- Home rows from the previous successful refresh are not carried forward.
- If the selected host filter is Home, the visible row list is empty.

That exactly matches the observed `Home -> 0 -> Checking -> 200` behavior.

## Current paging improvement

At `3ed11ad`, active session paging is bounded:

```swift
public static let activeSessionMaxPages = 1
```

`DockSessionQuery.activeHuman` and `DockSessionQuery.activeAgents` both use that `maxPages`.

`AppServerDockClient.loadSessions(...)` stops after `maxPages`:

```swift
if let maxPages = query.maxPages, pageCount >= maxPages {
    cursor = nil
    break
}
```

This prevents the older active-Dock behavior where the app drained every active cursor from Home before finishing. Earlier in this same work session, an app-shaped full cursor drain against Home showed:

```text

  958 rows
  19324ms

  1300 rows
  66601ms
  then timed out at 90s before completion
```

That explains why the pre-`3ed11ad` experience was much worse. It does not fully solve the current UI problem because the current one-page Home request can still take about 4 to 6 seconds, and stale Home rows are still dropped while the new Home request is in flight.

# Relay Code Path

## `thread/list` mostly passes through history rows

`scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`:

```js
async function aggregateThreadList(config, params = {}) {
  const historyParams = clampThreadListParams(params);
  const history = await readHistoryThreadList(config, historyParams);
  const data = Array.isArray(history.data) ? history.data : [];
  const summaryCache = threadSummaryCacheForConfig(config);
  const dataWithSummaries = summaryCache.decorateRows(data);
  summaryCache.warmRows(data);
  const liveOverlay = history.liveOverlay || liveStatusCacheForConfig(config).liveOverlay();
  return {
    ...history,
    data: dataWithSummaries,
    liveOverlay,
  };
}
```

What this means:

- The relay asks the raw history app-server for `thread/list`.
- It decorates row summaries.
- It warms summaries in the background.
- It attaches `liveOverlay`.
- It does not replace row status with live status.
- It does not insert loaded live rows into the list.
- It does not keep a cached stable host snapshot for the client.

## Live discovery is separate

`scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` discovers live loopback app-server processes:

```js
const endpoints = discoverLoopbackEndpoints()
  .filter((endpoint) => !excludedURLs.has(canonicalURLString(endpoint.url)));
```

It then calls:

```js
thread/loaded/list
thread/read
```

against those live endpoints and builds a live status cache.

The important Home result was:

```text
Home liveStatus.endpoints: 0
Home liveStatus.rows: 0
```

The important Amir-M5 result was:

```text
Amir-M5 liveStatus.endpoints: 2
Amir-M5 liveStatus.rows: 10
```

If Home is expected to have live Codex sessions, the next investigation should ask why the relay sees zero non-history loopback app-server processes on Home. The relay's discovery regex only sees process lines shaped like:

```text
codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:<port>
```

If Home's active sessions are launched under a different command shape, different user, container, service manager, or socket shape, this discovery path will miss them.

## Current relay tests protect "do not merge live status into list"

`scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` has a test named:

```text
relay thread/list keeps history status while focused detail can still route live
```

The test sets up:

- live row status: `active`
- history row status: `notLoaded`

Then it asserts the list row still says:

```js
assert.equal(rows[0].status.type, "notLoaded");
```

Plain meaning: the relay behavior that makes the Dock list mostly `Not loaded` is not accidental in the current codebase. It is an intentional contract today. The relay can route detail calls to the live owner, but the list remains history-first.

# Raw Codex App-Server Code Path

The upstream Codex app-server source confirms that `notLoaded` is a real state with a narrow meaning.

`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/README.md`:

```text
thread/list ... Each returned thread includes status (ThreadStatus), defaulting to notLoaded when the thread is not currently loaded.
```

The same README says:

```text
thread/loaded/list - list the thread ids currently loaded in memory.
```

`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs`:

```rust
status: ThreadStatus::NotLoaded,
```

is the default status assigned when a stored thread is converted into a `Thread`.

Then `thread/list` asks the thread watch manager for loaded statuses:

```rust
let statuses = self
    .thread_watch_manager
    .loaded_statuses_for_threads(status_ids)
    .await;
...
if let Some(status) = statuses.get(&thread.id) {
    thread.status = status.clone();
}
```

`/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs`:

```rust
fn loaded_status_for_thread(&self, thread_id: &str) -> ThreadStatus {
    self.status_for(thread_id)
        .unwrap_or(ThreadStatus::NotLoaded)
}
```

and:

```rust
fn loaded_thread_status(runtime: &RuntimeFacts) -> ThreadStatus {
    if !runtime.is_loaded {
        return ThreadStatus::NotLoaded;
    }
    ...
}
```

Plain meaning: upstream `notLoaded` does not mean "this row is missing basic list data." It means "this thread is not currently loaded in this app-server process's runtime memory."

# Root Cause

## Root cause 1: destructive partial snapshots

The Home zero-row behavior is a client state-management bug.

The Dock should treat a refresh as "new data is being fetched for a host." Instead, it treats a still-checking host as "this host currently contributes no rows." That is why a Home filter can collapse to zero even though the app had good Home rows from the previous refresh.

This is exposed by Home because Home is slower. Amir-M5 is fast enough that its partial period is tiny from the user's point of view.

## Root cause 2: `Not loaded` is technically true but product-hostile as a primary row badge

The upstream meaning is precise: the thread exists in history, but it is not currently loaded in a runtime owner.

For Dock, that status is not very useful as the dominant row state because most history rows will naturally be `notLoaded`. The row still has useful data:

- title or preview
- cwd/repository
- branch
- last activity
- source type
- host

So the row is not "not loaded" in the way a user reads that phrase. It is only "runtime status not loaded."

## Root cause 3: the relay leaves too much list assembly burden on the client

The relay currently gives the client:

- history pages from `thread/list`
- a separate `liveOverlay`
- live routing for detail operations

It does not give the client:

- a stable per-host Dock snapshot
- a stale-while-refresh contract
- merged live statuses for list rows
- a server-side answer to "show me the current Dock list for this host"

So the client is forced to fan out and rebuild the Dock view from lower-level pieces. That is workable for a fast single host. It is brittle when one host is slower and the UI needs stable filtered views.

## Root cause 4: Home has no discovered live rows

Home's live status cache reported:

```text
endpoints: 0
rows: 0
```

That means Home cannot currently upgrade list status from live app-server owners through the relay's live discovery path. This may be expected if Home has no live Codex sessions. If Home does have live sessions, this is a separate relay discovery problem.

# What Is Not The Root Cause

## Not raw connectivity

Both relays responded to `/statusz`. Both relays served `thread/list`. Simulator logs repeatedly recovered to:

```text
Online message=2 hosts online
```

## Not overlapping refreshes

The refresh loop awaits each refresh, then sleeps 5 seconds. There is no evidence that the app is starting a new Dock refresh before the previous one completes in normal foreground operation.

## Not a Swift string-only bug

The Swift mapper maps upstream `notLoaded` to the Dock row status:

```swift
case .notLoaded:
    return .notLoaded
```

The row projector then displays:

```swift
case .notLoaded:
    return .notLoaded
```

The label is confusing, but the data starts upstream.

## Not only the old Home checkout

Earlier, Home was running old code and that was a real confounder. Current evidence after syncing Home to `3ed11ad` still shows:

- Home requests are much slower than Amir-M5.
- Home rows disappear during partial refresh.
- all current list rows return `notLoaded`.

# UX Meaning

The UI should distinguish these concepts:

```text
Host reachability:
  Is the host online?

Host refresh state:
  Are we refreshing this host right now?

Row runtime status:
  Is this thread currently loaded/running/idle in a live app-server?

Row list availability:
  Do we have enough data to show the row in the Dock list?
```

Today those concepts are collapsed in the user's experience:

- A refreshing host looks like it temporarily has no rows.
- A history row whose runtime owner is not loaded looks like the row itself is "not loaded."
- A slow host looks unstable even when it is online.

# Candidate Fixes For Discussion Only

No fix was applied in this investigation pass.

## Option A: client stale-while-refresh per host

Keep each host's last successful rows while a new refresh for that host is in flight.

During refresh:

```text
Home: 200 sessions, refreshing
Rows: still visible from last successful Home snapshot
```

When Home finishes:

```text
Home: 200 sessions
Rows: replaced with fresh Home rows
```

This directly fixes the zero-row flicker. It is probably the smallest product-correct fix for the current symptom.

Primary simulator test requirement:

- Configure two hosts.
- Make one host slow enough to finish after the other.
- Select/filter the slow host after an initial successful load.
- Trigger refresh.
- Verify the slow host keeps its previous rows while its host state indicates refresh/checking.

If current simulator hooks cannot force a slow host, add hooks. This should not rely on unit tests as the primary proof.

## Option B: split `checking` from `refreshing`

Use `checking` for first load or unknown host state only.

Use `refreshing` when the host already has a last-good snapshot.

This makes the UI language match reality:

```text
First load:
  Home: Checking
  Rows: none yet

Later refresh:
  Home: Refreshing
  Rows: retained
```

This is strongly related to Option A and may be part of the same client fix.

## Option C: relay-level Dock snapshot endpoint

Add a relay-owned endpoint shaped for the Dock, for example:

```text
dock/snapshot
```

The relay would own:

- history paging policy
- status merge policy
- stale-while-refresh behavior
- per-host caching
- live status integration

The client would ask for the current host snapshot instead of rebuilding everything from lower-level history and live endpoints.

This is a bigger architectural fix, but it fits the product direction better if the relay is meant to simplify the phone client.

Primary simulator test requirement:

- App connected to real relay.
- Relay snapshot refresh in progress.
- Host-filtered UI remains stable.
- Offline/error states still render correctly when the host path is unavailable.

## Option D: relay merges live status into `thread/list` rows

The relay already knows about live rows on Amir-M5. It could replace `notLoaded` status on matching list rows when a live row exists.

This would change an existing protected behavior. `scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` currently asserts that history status wins for `thread/list`, even when live detail routing is available.

So this is not a trivial cleanup. It is a product/API contract decision.

## Option E: reduce `Not loaded` prominence

Even if upstream keeps `notLoaded`, the Dock row badge does not have to present it as the main row status.

Possible UX interpretations:

- Show no status badge for `notLoaded` history rows.
- Show `History` instead of `Not loaded`.
- Show runtime statuses only when they are meaningful: `Running`, `Needs input`, `Error`, maybe `Idle`.
- Move `Not loaded` into a debug/detail field or filter, not the default row badge.

This does not fix the Home zero-row flicker, but it addresses the "everything says Not loaded" product problem.

## Option F: investigate Home live discovery

If Home is expected to have active Codex sessions, inspect why the relay sees:

```text
liveStatus.endpoints: 0
liveStatus.rows: 0
```

The likely checks:

```bash
ps -axo pid,command | rg 'codex app-server --listen ws://127\\.0\\.0\\.1:'
```

and whether Home sessions are launched:

- under the same user as the relay
- with a different command shape
- in a container namespace
- through a non-loopback socket
- without `codex app-server --listen ...`

This is separate from the client stale-row bug. Fixing live discovery would make statuses more useful, but it would not by itself stop stale Home rows from disappearing during refresh.

# Recommended Direction

The clean product path is probably:

1. Fix the client to retain last-good host rows during refresh.
2. Rename the refresh state so first load is `Checking` and later refresh is visibly different.
3. Decide whether `Not loaded` should remain a visible row status at all.
4. Separately decide whether the relay should provide a Dock-shaped snapshot or merge live statuses into list rows.
5. Investigate Home live discovery only if Home should have active live sessions right now.

The first fix should be simulator-proven. A unit test can cover the state reducer behavior, but it should not be treated as completion evidence. The important proof is the visible simulator behavior with a slow host selected.

574	        guard !isLoading else {
575	            DockLog.dock.debug("dock reload skipped reason=already_loading")

577	        }

579	        let startedAt = Date()
580	        let signpostState = DockSignpost.dock.beginInterval("dock.reload")
581	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock reload started hosts=\(self.hosts.count, privacy: .public) show_loading=\(showLoading, privacy: .public)")
582	        isLoading = true
583	        defer {
584	            DockSignpost.dock.endInterval("dock.reload", signpostState)
585	            isLoading = false
586	        }

588	        let hostViewModels = hosts.map(DockHostViewModel.init)
589	        let primaryHostViewModel = hostViewModels[0]
590	        if showLoading {
591	            state = .loading(hostViewModels)
592	            connectivityReporter?.reportDockState(state)

598	        } catch {

601	        }

603	        let results = await loadAllHostsPublishingPartial()
604	        let snapshot = makeSnapshot(results: results)
605	
606	        if hosts.count == 1, let first = results.first {
607	            if let failure = first.completeFailure {
608	                switch failure {
609	                case .offline(let message):
610	                    state = .offline(primaryHostViewModel, message)
611	                case .error(let message):
612	                    state = .error(primaryHostViewModel, message)
613	                }
614	            } else {
615	                state = .loaded(snapshot)
616	            }
617	        } else {
618	            state = .loaded(snapshot)
619	        }
620	        connectivityReporter?.reportDockState(state)
621	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock reload finished hosts=\(self.hosts.count, privacy: .public) rows=\(snapshot.rowCount, privacy: .public) mapping_failures=\(snapshot.mappingFailures.count, privacy: .public) scope_failures=\(snapshot.scopeLoadFailures.count, privacy: .public) conflicts=\(snapshot.scopeConflicts.count, privacy: .public) duration_ms=\(DockLog.milliseconds(since: startedAt), privacy: .public)")
622	    }

639	    private struct HostLoadOutcome: Sendable {
640	        let host: DockHostConfiguration
641	        let scopedResults: [ScopedHostLoadOutcome]
642	
643	        var completeFailure: DockLoadFailure? {
644	            let failures = scopedResults.compactMap { outcome -> DockLoadFailure? in
645	                if case .failure(let failure) = outcome.result {
646	                    return failure
647	                }
648	                return nil
649	            }
650	            guard !scopedResults.isEmpty, failures.count == scopedResults.count else {
651	                return nil
652	            }
653	            if let error = failures.first(where: { failure in
654	                if case .error = failure {
655	                    return true
656	                }
657	                return false
658	            }) {
659	                return error
660	            }
661	            return failures[0]
662	        }
663	    }

665	    private func loadAllHostsPublishingPartial() async -> [HostLoadOutcome] {
666	        await withTaskGroup(of: HostLoadOutcome.self) { group in
667	            for host in hosts {
668	                group.addTask { [loader] in
669	                    let scopedResults = await Self.loadActiveScopes(loader: loader, host: host)
670	                    return HostLoadOutcome(host: host, scopedResults: scopedResults)
671	                }
672	            }
673	
674	            var outcomes: [HostLoadOutcome] = []
675	            var checkingHostIDs = Set(hosts.map(\.id))
676	            for await outcome in group {
677	                outcomes.append(outcome)
678	                checkingHostIDs.remove(outcome.host.id)
679	                outcomes.sort { lhs, rhs in
680	                    hostIndex(lhs.host.id) < hostIndex(rhs.host.id)
681	                }
682	                if !checkingHostIDs.isEmpty {
683	                    state = .loaded(makeSnapshot(results: outcomes, checkingHostIDs: checkingHostIDs))
684	                    connectivityReporter?.reportDockState(state)
685	                }
686	            }
687	            return outcomes.sorted { lhs, rhs in
688	                hostIndex(lhs.host.id) < hostIndex(rhs.host.id)
689	            }
690	        }
691	    }

693	    private nonisolated static func loadActiveScopes(
694	        loader: any DockSessionLoading,
695	        host: DockHostConfiguration
696	    ) async -> [ScopedHostLoadOutcome] {
697	        await withTaskGroup(of: ScopedHostLoadOutcome.self) { group in
698	            for scope in DockSessionScope.allCases {
699	                group.addTask { [loader] in
700	                    ScopedHostLoadOutcome(
701	                        scope: scope,
702	                        result: await Self.loadScope(
703	                            loader: loader,
704	                            host: host,
705	                            query: scope.query
706	                        )
707	                    )
708	                }
709	            }
710	
711	            var outcomes: [ScopedHostLoadOutcome] = []
712	            for await outcome in group {
713	                outcomes.append(outcome)
714	            }
715	            return outcomes.sorted { lhs, rhs in
716	                Self.scopeIndex(lhs.scope) < Self.scopeIndex(rhs.scope)
717	            }
718	        }
719	    }

721	    private nonisolated static func loadScope(
722	        loader: any DockSessionLoading,
723	        host: DockHostConfiguration,
724	        query: DockSessionQuery
725	    ) async -> Result<DockLoadResult, DockLoadFailure> {
726	        let startedAt = Date()
727	        let scope = DockSessionScope.allCases.first { $0.query == query }?.rawValue ?? "custom"
728	        DockLog.dock.debug("dock scope load started host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) scope=\(scope, privacy: .public)")
729	        do {
730	            let result = try await loader.loadSessions(for: host, query: query)
731	            DockLog.dock.debug("dock scope load finished host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) scope=\(scope, privacy: .public) rows=\(result.summaries.count, privacy: .public) mapping_failures=\(result.mappingFailures.count, privacy: .public) duration_ms=\(DockLog.milliseconds(since: startedAt), privacy: .public)")
732	            return .success(result)
733	        } catch {
734	            DockLog.dock.warning("dock scope load failed host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) scope=\(scope, privacy: .public) duration_ms=\(DockLog.milliseconds(since: startedAt), privacy: .public) error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
735	            return .failure(mapLoadFailure(error))
736	        }
737	    }

739	    private nonisolated static func mapLoadFailure(_ error: Error) -> DockLoadFailure {
740	        if let failure = error as? DockLoadFailure {
741	            return failure
742	        }
743	        return .error(error.localizedDescription)
744	    }

746	    private func makeSnapshot(
747	        results: [HostLoadOutcome],
748	        checkingHostIDs: Set<String> = []
749	    ) -> DockSnapshot {
750	        var summaries: [SessionSummary] = []
751	        var mappingFailures: [SessionSummaryMappingFailure] = []
752	        var hostStatesByID: [String: DockHostStateViewModel] = [:]
753	        var scopeLoadFailures: [DockScopeLoadFailureViewModel] = []
754	        var scopeConflicts: [DockScopeConflictViewModel] = []
755	
756	        for outcome in results {
757	            let host = DockHostViewModel(host: outcome.host)
758	            let hostSummaries = successfulScopedSummaries(from: outcome)
759	            let deduplicated = deduplicated(hostSummaries)
760	            let hostDedupedSummaries = deduplicated.summaries
761	            let overlayMessages = successfulLiveOverlayMessages(from: outcome)
762	            summaries.append(contentsOf: hostDedupedSummaries)
763	            scopeConflicts.append(contentsOf: deduplicated.conflicts)
764	            mappingFailures.append(contentsOf: successfulMappingFailures(from: outcome))
765	
766	            for scopedOutcome in outcome.scopedResults {
767	                if case .failure(let failure) = scopedOutcome.result {
768	                    scopeLoadFailures.append(
769	                        DockScopeLoadFailureViewModel(
770	                            host: host,
771	                            scope: scopedOutcome.scope,
772	                            message: failure.localizedDescription
773	                        )
774	                    )
775	                }
776	            }
777	
778	            if let failure = outcome.completeFailure {
779	                switch failure {
780	                case .offline(let message):
781	                    hostStatesByID[host.id] = DockHostStateViewModel(host: host, status: .offline(message))
782	                case .error(let message):
783	                    hostStatesByID[host.id] = DockHostStateViewModel(host: host, status: .error(message))
784	                }
785	            } else if scopeLoadFailures.contains(where: { $0.host.id == host.id }) {
786	                var messages = scopeLoadFailures
787	                    .filter { $0.host.id == host.id }
788	                    .map { "\($0.scope.label): \($0.message)" }
789	                messages.append(contentsOf: overlayMessages)
790	                hostStatesByID[host.id] =
791	                    DockHostStateViewModel(
792	                        host: host,
793	                        status: .partial(rowCount: hostDedupedSummaries.count, message: messages.joined(separator: "; "))
794	                    )
795	            } else if !overlayMessages.isEmpty {
796	                hostStatesByID[host.id] =
797	                    DockHostStateViewModel(
798	                        host: host,
799	                        status: .partial(
800	                            rowCount: hostDedupedSummaries.count,
801	                            message: overlayMessages.joined(separator: "; ")
802	                        )
803	                    )
804	            } else {
805	                hostStatesByID[host.id] =
806	                    DockHostStateViewModel(
807	                        host: host,
808	                        status: hostDedupedSummaries.isEmpty
809	                            ? .empty
810	                            : .loaded(rowCount: hostDedupedSummaries.count)
811	                    )
812	            }
813	        }
814	
815	        for host in hosts where checkingHostIDs.contains(host.id) {
816	            let hostViewModel = DockHostViewModel(host: host)
817	            hostStatesByID[host.id] = DockHostStateViewModel(host: hostViewModel, status: .checking)
818	        }
819	
820	        let projector = SessionRowProjector(
821	            hosts: hosts,
822	            localMetadata: localMetadata,
823	            now: now
824	        )
825	        let rows = projector.rows(from: summaries)
826	
827	        return DockSnapshot(
828	            host: DockHostViewModel(host: hosts[0]),
829	            hosts: hosts.map(DockHostViewModel.init),
830	            hostStates: hosts.compactMap { hostStatesByID[$0.id] },
831	            rows: rows,
832	            scopeLoadFailures: scopeLoadFailures,
833	            scopeConflicts: scopeConflicts,
834	            mappingFailures: mappingFailures,
835	            isPartial: !checkingHostIDs.isEmpty
836	        )
837	    }
838	
839	    private func successfulScopedSummaries(from outcome: HostLoadOutcome) -> [ScopedSessionSummary] {
840	        var summaries: [ScopedSessionSummary] = []
841	        for scopedOutcome in outcome.scopedResults {
842	            if case .success(let result) = scopedOutcome.result {
843	                summaries.append(
844	                    contentsOf: result.summaries.map { summary in
845	                        ScopedSessionSummary(scope: scopedOutcome.scope, summary: summary)
846	                    }
847	                )
848	            }
849	        }
850	        return summaries
851	    }
852	
853	    private func successfulLiveOverlayMessages(from outcome: HostLoadOutcome) -> [String] {
854	        var messages: [String] = []
855	        for scopedOutcome in outcome.scopedResults {
856	            guard case .success(let result) = scopedOutcome.result,
857	                  let message = result.liveOverlay?.degradedMessage,
858	                  !messages.contains(message) else {
859	                continue
860	            }
861	            messages.append(message)
862	        }
863	        return messages
864	    }
865	
866	    private func successfulMappingFailures(from outcome: HostLoadOutcome) -> [SessionSummaryMappingFailure] {
867	        var failures: [SessionSummaryMappingFailure] = []
868	        for scopedOutcome in outcome.scopedResults {
869	            if case .success(let result) = scopedOutcome.result {
870	                failures.append(contentsOf: result.mappingFailures)
871	            }
872	        }
873	        return failures
874	    }
875	
876	    private func deduplicated(_ summaries: [ScopedSessionSummary]) -> DeduplicatedSummaries {
877	        var orderedIDs: [HostScopedThreadID] = []
878	        var summariesByID: [HostScopedThreadID: SessionSummary] = [:]
879	        var scopesByID: [HostScopedThreadID: Set<DockSessionScope>] = [:]
880	        var conflictIDs: Set<HostScopedThreadID> = []
881	        var conflicts: [DockScopeConflictViewModel] = []
882	
883	        for scopedSummary in summaries {
884	            let summary = scopedSummary.summary
885	            if summariesByID[summary.id] == nil {
886	                orderedIDs.append(summary.id)
887	                summariesByID[summary.id] = summary
888	                scopesByID[summary.id] = [scopedSummary.scope]
889	                continue

892	            guard let existing = summariesByID[summary.id] else {
893	                continue
894	            }
895	            var scopes = scopesByID[summary.id] ?? []
896	            if !scopes.contains(scopedSummary.scope), !conflictIDs.contains(summary.id) {
897	                conflictIDs.insert(summary.id)

899	                conflicts.append(

106	        var cursor: String?
107	        var seenCursors = Set<String>()
108	        var summaries: [SessionSummary] = []
109	        var mappingFailures: [SessionSummaryMappingFailure] = []
110	        var backwardsCursor: String?
111	        var nextCursor: String?
112	        var liveOverlay: ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO?
113	        var pageCount = 0
114	
115	        repeat {
116	            let response = try await client.threadList(
117	                params: ThreadListParams(
118	                    cursor: cursor,
119	                    limit: pageLimit(for: query),
120	                    sortKey: .updatedAt,
121	                    sortDirection: .desc,
122	                    modelProviders: [],
123	                    sourceKinds: query.sourceKinds,
124	                    archived: query.archived

127	            )

129	            summaries.append(contentsOf: mapped.summaries)
130	            mappingFailures.append(contentsOf: mapped.failures)
131	            backwardsCursor = backwardsCursor ?? response.backwardsCursor
132	            nextCursor = response.nextCursor
133	            liveOverlay = combineLiveOverlay(current: liveOverlay, next: response.liveOverlay)
134	            pageCount += 1
135	
136	            if let maxPages = query.maxPages, pageCount >= maxPages {
137	                cursor = nil
138	                break
139	            }
140	
141	            guard let next = response.nextCursor, !next.isEmpty else {
142	                cursor = nil
143	                break
144	            }
145	            guard seenCursors.insert(next).inserted else {
146	                throw DockLoadFailure.error("Relay returned repeated thread/list cursor \(next)")
147	            }
148	            cursor = next
149	        } while cursor != nil
150

153	            mappingFailures: mappingFailures,
154	            nextCursor: nextCursor,
155	            backwardsCursor: backwardsCursor,
156	            liveOverlay: liveOverlay

199	    ) async throws -> Value {

203	            }

205	            throw mapLoadFailure(error)

212	        }
213	
214	        if let clientError = error as? AppServerClientError {
215	            switch clientError {

218	            case .duplicateRequestID,

226	            }
227	        }

50	        maxAttempts: Int,

52	        maxDelayMilliseconds: Int,
53	        jitterRatio: Double = 0.0
54	    ) {
55	        precondition(maxAttempts > 0, "Reconnect attempts must be positive")
56	        precondition(initialDelayMilliseconds >= 0, "Initial reconnect delay cannot be negative")
57	        precondition(maxDelayMilliseconds >= initialDelayMilliseconds, "Max reconnect delay must cover initial delay")
58	        precondition(jitterRatio >= 0, "Reconnect jitter cannot be negative")
59	        self.maxAttempts = maxAttempts
60	        self.initialDelayMilliseconds = initialDelayMilliseconds
61	        self.maxDelayMilliseconds = maxDelayMilliseconds
62	        self.jitterRatio = jitterRatio
63	    }

65	    func delay(for attempt: Int) -> Duration {
66	        let exponent = max(0, min(attempt - 1, CodexDockConstants.AppServer.maximumBackoffExponent))
67	        let multiplier = 1 << exponent
68	        let baseDelay = min(maxDelayMilliseconds, initialDelayMilliseconds * multiplier)
69	        let jitterWindow = Int(Double(baseDelay) * jitterRatio)
70	        let jitter = jitterWindow > 0 ? Int.random(in: -jitterWindow...jitterWindow) : 0
71	        return .milliseconds(max(0, baseDelay + jitter))
72	    }

79	    private let agentSessionPageLimit = CodexDockConstants.Dock.agentSessionPageLimit
80	
81	    public init() {}
82	
83	    public func loadSessions(
84	        for host: DockHostConfiguration,
85	        query: DockSessionQuery
86	    ) async throws -> DockLoadResult {
87	        let startedAt = Date()
88	        let sourceKinds = query.sourceKinds?.map(\.rawValue).joined(separator: ",")
89	        DockLog.dock.info("dock client load started host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) endpoint=\(DockLog.endpoint(host.webSocketURL), privacy: .public) archived=\(query.archived, privacy: .public) source_kinds=\(DockLog.publicID(sourceKinds), privacy: .public)")
90	        return try await withClient(for: host) { client in
91	            let result = try await loadSessions(
92	                using: client,
93	                hostID: host.id,
94	                query: query
95	            )
96	            DockLog.dock.info("dock client load finished host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) archived=\(query.archived, privacy: .public) rows=\(result.summaries.count, privacy: .public) mapping_failures=\(result.mappingFailures.count, privacy: .public) duration_ms=\(DockLog.milliseconds(since: startedAt), privacy: .public)")
97	            return result
98	        }
99	    }
100	
101	    func loadSessions(
102	        using client: AppServerClient,
103	        hostID: String,
104	        query: DockSessionQuery
105	    ) async throws -> DockLoadResult {
106	        var cursor: String?
107	        var seenCursors = Set<String>()
108	        var summaries: [SessionSummary] = []
109	        var mappingFailures: [SessionSummaryMappingFailure] = []
110	        var backwardsCursor: String?
111	        var nextCursor: String?
112	        var liveOverlay: ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO?
113	        var pageCount = 0
114	
115	        repeat {
116	            let response = try await client.threadList(
117	                params: ThreadListParams(
118	                    cursor: cursor,
119	                    limit: pageLimit(for: query),
120	                    sortKey: .updatedAt,
121	                    sortDirection: .desc,
122	                    modelProviders: [],
123	                    sourceKinds: query.sourceKinds,
124	                    archived: query.archived
125	                ),
126	                timeout: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.defaultRequestTimeout
127	            )
128	            let mapped = SessionSummaryMapper.map(response: response, hostID: hostID)
129	            summaries.append(contentsOf: mapped.summaries)
130	            mappingFailures.append(contentsOf: mapped.failures)
131	            backwardsCursor = backwardsCursor ?? response.backwardsCursor
132	            nextCursor = response.nextCursor
133	            liveOverlay = combineLiveOverlay(current: liveOverlay, next: response.liveOverlay)
134	            pageCount += 1
135	
136	            if let maxPages = query.maxPages, pageCount >= maxPages {
137	                cursor = nil
138	                break
139	            }
140	
141	            guard let next = response.nextCursor, !next.isEmpty else {
142	                cursor = nil
143	                break
144	            }
145	            guard seenCursors.insert(next).inserted else {
146	                throw DockLoadFailure.error("Relay returned repeated thread/list cursor \(next)")
147	            }
148	            cursor = next
149	        } while cursor != nil
150	
151	        return DockLoadResult(
152	            summaries: summaries,
153	            mappingFailures: mappingFailures,
154	            nextCursor: nextCursor,
155	            backwardsCursor: backwardsCursor,
156	            liveOverlay: liveOverlay
157	        )
158	    }

161	        query == .activeAgents ? agentSessionPageLimit : humanSessionPageLimit
162	    }

164	    private func combineLiveOverlay(
165	        current: ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO?,
166	        next: ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO?
167	    ) -> ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO? {
168	        guard let next else {
169	            return current
170	        }
171	        return next
172	    }

175	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock archive started host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(threadID), privacy: .public)")
176	        _ = try await withClient(for: host) { client in

179	                timeout: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.defaultRequestTimeout
180	            )
181	        }
182	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock archive finished host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(threadID), privacy: .public)")
183	    }

185	    public func unarchiveThread(_ threadID: String, on host: DockHostConfiguration) async throws {
186	        DockLog.archive.notice("archive restore started host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(threadID), privacy: .public)")
187	        _ = try await withClient(for: host) { client in
188	            try await client.threadUnarchive(
189	                params: ThreadUnarchiveParams(threadId: threadID),
190	                timeout: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.defaultRequestTimeout
191	            )
192	        }
193	        DockLog.archive.notice("archive restore finished host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(threadID), privacy: .public)")
194	    }
195	
196	    private func withClient<Value>(
197	        for host: DockHostConfiguration,
198	        operation: @Sendable (AppServerClient) async throws -> Value
199	    ) async throws -> Value {
200	        do {
201	            return try await AppServerHostConnector().withConnectedClient(for: host) { connection in
202	                try await operation(connection.client)
203	            }
204	        } catch {
205	            throw mapLoadFailure(error)
206	        }
207	    }

209	    private func mapLoadFailure(_ error: Error) -> DockLoadFailure {
