1	# codex-app-server
2	
3	`codex app-server` is the interface Codex uses to power rich interfaces such as the [Codex VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=openai.chatgpt).
4	
5	## Table of Contents
6	
7	- [Protocol](#protocol)
8	- [Message Schema](#message-schema)
9	- [Core Primitives](#core-primitives)
10	- [Lifecycle Overview](#lifecycle-overview)
11	- [Initialization](#initialization)
12	- [API Overview](#api-overview)
13	- [Events](#events)
14	- [Approvals](#approvals)
15	- [Skills](#skills)
16	- [Apps](#apps)
17	- [Auth endpoints](#auth-endpoints)
18	- [Experimental API Opt-in](#experimental-api-opt-in)
19	
20	## Protocol
21	
22	Similar to [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/), `codex app-server` supports bidirectional communication using JSON-RPC 2.0 messages (with the `"jsonrpc":"2.0"` header omitted on the wire).
23	
24	Supported transports:
25	
26	- stdio (`--listen stdio://`, default): newline-delimited JSON (JSONL)
27	- websocket (`--listen ws://IP:PORT`): one JSON-RPC message per websocket text frame (**experimental / unsupported**)
28	- unix socket (`--listen unix://` or `--listen unix://PATH`): websocket connections over `$CODEX_HOME/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock` or a custom socket path, using the standard HTTP Upgrade handshake
29	- off (`--listen off`): do not expose a local transport
30	
31	When running with `--listen ws://IP:PORT`, the same listener also serves basic HTTP health probes:
32	
33	- `GET /readyz` returns `200 OK` once the listener is accepting new connections.
34	- `GET /healthz` returns `200 OK` when no `Origin` header is present.
35	- Any request carrying an `Origin` header is rejected with `403 Forbidden`.
36	
37	Websocket transport is currently experimental and unsupported. Do not rely on it for production workloads.
38	
39	The unix socket transport is intended for local app-server control-plane clients. `codex app-server proxy`
40	opens exactly one raw stream connection to `$CODEX_HOME/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock`
41	by default, or to `--sock PATH` when provided, and proxies bytes between that socket and stdin/stdout.
42	The proxied stream carries the websocket HTTP Upgrade handshake followed by websocket frames.
43	
44	Tracing/log output:
45	
46	- `RUST_LOG` controls log filtering/verbosity.
47	- Set `LOG_FORMAT=json` to emit app-server tracing logs to `stderr` as JSON (one event per line).
48	
49	Backpressure behavior:
50	
51	- The server uses bounded queues between transport ingress, request processing, and outbound writes.
52	- When request ingress is saturated, new requests are rejected with a JSON-RPC error code `-32001` and message `"Server overloaded; retry later."`.
53	- Clients should treat this as retryable and use exponential backoff with jitter.
54	
55	## Message Schema
56	
57	Currently, you can dump a TypeScript version of the schema using `codex app-server generate-ts`, or a JSON Schema bundle via `codex app-server generate-json-schema`. Each output is specific to the version of Codex you used to run the command, so the generated artifacts are guaranteed to match that version.
58	
59	```
60	codex app-server generate-ts --out DIR
61	codex app-server generate-json-schema --out DIR
62	```
63	
64	## Core Primitives
65	
66	The API exposes three top level primitives representing an interaction between a user and Codex:
67	
68	- **Thread**: A conversation between a user and the Codex agent. Each thread contains multiple turns.
69	- **Turn**: One turn of the conversation, typically starting with a user message and finishing with an agent message. Each turn contains multiple items.
70	- **Item**: Represents user inputs and agent outputs as part of the turn, persisted and used as the context for future conversations. Example items include user message, agent reasoning, agent message, shell command, file edit, etc.
71	
72	Use the thread APIs to create, list, or archive conversations. Drive a conversation with turn APIs and stream progress via turn notifications.
73	
74	## Lifecycle Overview
75	
76	- Initialize once per connection: Immediately after opening a transport connection, send an `initialize` request with your client metadata, then emit an `initialized` notification. Any other request on that connection before this handshake gets rejected.
77	- Start (or resume) a thread: Call `thread/start` to open a fresh conversation. The response returns the thread object and you’ll also get a `thread/started` notification. If you’re continuing an existing conversation, call `thread/resume` with its ID instead. If you want to branch from an existing conversation, call `thread/fork` to create a new thread id with copied history. Like `thread/start`, `thread/fork` also accepts `ephemeral: true` for an in-memory temporary thread.
78	  The returned `thread.ephemeral` flag tells you whether the session is intentionally in-memory only; when it is `true`, `thread.path` is `null`.
79	- Begin a turn: To send user input, call `turn/start` with the target `threadId` and the user's input. Optional fields let you override model, cwd, sandbox policy or experimental `permissions` profile selection, approval policy, approvals reviewer, etc. This immediately returns the new turn object. The app-server emits `turn/started` when that turn actually begins running.
80	- Stream events: After `turn/start`, keep reading JSON-RPC notifications on stdout. You’ll see `item/started`, `item/completed`, deltas like `item/agentMessage/delta`, tool progress, etc. These represent streaming model output plus any side effects (commands, tool calls, reasoning notes).
81	- Finish the turn: When the model is done (or the turn is interrupted via making the `turn/interrupt` call), the server sends `turn/completed` with the final turn state and token usage.
82	
83	## Initialization
84	
85	Clients must send a single `initialize` request per transport connection before invoking any other method on that connection, then acknowledge with an `initialized` notification. The server returns the user agent string it will present to upstream services, `codexHome` for the server's Codex home directory, and `platformFamily` and `platformOs` strings describing the app-server runtime target; subsequent requests issued before initialization receive a `"Not initialized"` error, and repeated `initialize` calls on the same connection receive an `"Already initialized"` error.
86	
87	`initialize.params.capabilities` also supports per-connection notification opt-out via `optOutNotificationMethods`, which is a list of exact method names to suppress for that connection. Matching is exact (no wildcards/prefixes). Unknown method names are accepted and ignored.
88	
89	Applications building on top of `codex app-server` should identify themselves via the `clientInfo` parameter.
90	
91	**Important**: `clientInfo.name` is used to identify the client for the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform. If
92	you are developing a new Codex integration that is intended for enterprise use, please contact us to get it
93	added to a known clients list. For more context: https://chatgpt.com/admin/api-reference#tag/Logs:-Codex
94	
95	Example (from OpenAI's official VSCode extension):
96	
97	```json
98	{
99	  "method": "initialize",
100	  "id": 0,
101	  "params": {
102	    "clientInfo": {
103	      "name": "codex_vscode",
104	      "title": "Codex VS Code Extension",
105	      "version": "0.1.0"
106	    }
107	  }
108	}
109	```
110	
111	Example with notification opt-out:
112	
113	```json
114	{
115	  "method": "initialize",
116	  "id": 1,
117	  "params": {
118	    "clientInfo": {
119	      "name": "my_client",
120	      "title": "My Client",
121	      "version": "0.1.0"
122	    },
123	    "capabilities": {
124	      "experimentalApi": true,
125	      "optOutNotificationMethods": ["thread/started", "item/agentMessage/delta"]
126	    }
127	  }
128	}
129	```
130

205	- `plugin/read` — read one plugin by `marketplacePath` plus `pluginName`, returning marketplace info, a list-style `summary`, manifest descriptions/interface metadata, and bundled skills/hooks/apps/MCP server names. Returned plugin skills include their current `enabled` state after local config filtering; bundled hooks are returned as lightweight declaration summaries keyed for correlation with `hooks/list`. Plugin app summaries also include `needsAuth` when the server can determine connector accessibility (**under development; do not call from production clients yet**).
206	- `plugin/skill/read` — read remote plugin skill markdown on demand by `remoteMarketplaceName`, `remotePluginId`, and `skillName`. This lets clients preview uninstalled remote plugin skills without downloading the plugin bundle.
207	- `skills/changed` — notification emitted when watched local skill files change.
208	- `app/list` — list available apps.
209	- `remoteControl/enable` — experimental; enable remote control for the current app-server process and return the current remote-control status snapshot. The caller is responsible for persisting the desired setting outside app-server.
210	- `remoteControl/disable` — experimental; disable remote control for the current app-server process and return the current remote-control status snapshot. This does not revoke already enrolled controller devices.
211	- `remoteControl/status/read` — experimental; read the current remote-control status snapshot. `status` is one of `disabled`, `connecting`, `connected`, or `errored`; `serverName` is the local machine name used by this app-server process; `environmentId` is a string when the app-server has a current enrollment and `null` when that enrollment is cleared, invalidated, or remote control is disabled.
212	- `remoteControl/status/changed` — notification emitted when the remote-control status or client-visible environment id changes. `status` is one of `disabled`, `connecting`, `connected`, or `errored`; `serverName` is the local machine name used by this app-server process; `environmentId` is a string when the app-server has a current enrollment and `null` when that enrollment is cleared, invalidated, or remote control is disabled. Newly initialized app-server clients always receive the current status snapshot.
213	- `skills/config/write` — write user-level skill config by name or absolute path.
214	- `plugin/install` — install a plugin from a discovered marketplace entry, rejecting marketplace entries marked unavailable for install, install MCPs if any, and return the effective plugin auth policy plus any apps that still need auth (**under development; do not call from production clients yet**).
215	- `plugin/uninstall` — uninstall a local plugin by `pluginId` in `<plugin>@<marketplace>` form by removing its cached files and clearing its user-level config entry, or uninstall a remote ChatGPT plugin by backend `pluginId` by forwarding the uninstall to the ChatGPT plugin backend and removing any downloaded remote-plugin cache (**under development; do not call from production clients yet**).
216	- `mcpServer/oauth/login` — start an OAuth login for a configured MCP server; returns an `authorization_url` and later emits `mcpServer/oauthLogin/completed` once the browser flow finishes.
217	- `tool/requestUserInput` — prompt the user with 1–3 short questions for a tool call and return their answers (experimental).
218	- `config/mcpServer/reload` — reload MCP server config from disk and queue a refresh for loaded threads (applied on each thread's next active turn); returns `{}`. Use this after editing `config.toml` without restarting the server.
219	- `mcpServerStatus/list` — enumerate configured MCP servers with their tools and auth status, plus resources/resource templates for `full` detail; supports optional `threadId` and cursor+limit pagination. If `threadId` is omitted, the server reads from the latest global config directly. If `detail` is omitted, the server defaults to `full`.
220	- `mcpServer/resource/read` — read a resource from a configured MCP server by optional `threadId`, `server`, and `uri`, returning text/blob resource `contents`. If `threadId` is omitted, the server reads from the latest MCP config directly.
221	- `mcpServer/tool/call` — call a tool on a thread's configured MCP server by `threadId`, `server`, `tool`, optional `arguments`, and optional `_meta`, returning the MCP tool result.
222	- `windowsSandbox/setupStart` — start Windows sandbox setup for the selected mode (`elevated` or `unelevated`); accepts an optional absolute `cwd` to target setup for a specific workspace, returns `{ started: true }` immediately, and later emits `windowsSandbox/setupCompleted`.
223	- `feedback/upload` — submit a feedback report (classification + optional reason/logs, conversation_id, and optional `extraLogFiles` attachments array); returns the tracking thread id.
224	- `config/read` — fetch the effective config on disk after resolving config layering, including opaque `desktop` values stored in `config.toml`.
225	- `externalAgentConfig/detect` — detect migratable external-agent artifacts with `includeHome` and optional `cwds`; each detected item includes `cwd` (`null` for home), and plugin/session migration items may additionally include structured `details` grouping plugin ids or session metadata.
226	- `externalAgentConfig/import` — apply selected external-agent migration items by passing explicit `migrationItems` with `cwd` (`null` for home) and any plugin/session `details` returned by detect. When a request includes migration items, the server emits `externalAgentConfig/import/completed` once after the full import finishes (immediately after the response when everything completed synchronously, or after background imports finish).
227	- `config/value/write` — write a single config key/value to the user's config.toml on disk; dotted paths such as `desktop.someKey` use the same generic write surface.
228	- `config/batchWrite` — apply multiple config edits atomically to the user's config.toml on disk, with optional `reloadUserConfig: true` to hot-reload loaded threads, including multiple `desktop.*` edits.
229	- `configRequirements/read` — fetch loaded requirements constraints from `requirements.toml` and/or MDM (or `null` if none are configured), including allow-lists (`allowedApprovalPolicies`, `allowedSandboxModes`, `allowedWebSearchModes`, `allowedPermissions`), lifecycle hook lockdown (`allowManagedHooksOnly`), computer use policy (`computerUse`), pinned feature values (`featureRequirements`), managed lifecycle hooks (`hooks`), `enforceResidency`, and `network` constraints such as canonical domain/socket permissions plus `managedAllowedDomainsOnly` and `dangerFullAccessDenylistOnly`.
230	
231	### Example: Start or resume a thread
232	
233	Start a fresh thread when you need a new Codex conversation.
234	
235	```json
236	{ "method": "thread/start", "id": 10, "params": {
237	    // Optionally set config settings. If not specified, will use the user's
238	    // current config settings.
239	    "model": "gpt-5.1-codex",
240	    "cwd": "/Users/me/project",
241	    "approvalPolicy": "never",
242	    "sandbox": "workspaceWrite",
243	    // Prefer experimental profile selection:
244	    // "permissions": ":workspace"
245	    // Experimental runtime roots for :workspace_roots materialization:
246	    // "runtimeWorkspaceRoots": ["/Users/me/project", "/Users/me/openai"],
247	    // Do not send both "sandbox" and "permissions".
248	    "personality": "friendly",
249	    "serviceName": "my_app_server_client", // optional metrics tag (`service_name`)
250	    "sessionStartSource": "startup", // optional: "startup" (default) or "clear"
251	    // Experimental: requires opt-in
252	    "dynamicTools": [
253	        {
254	            "name": "lookup_ticket",
255	            "description": "Fetch a ticket by id",
256	            "deferLoading": true,
257	            "inputSchema": {
258	                "type": "object",
259	                "properties": {
260	                    "id": { "type": "string" }
261	                },
262	                "required": ["id"]
263	            }
264	        }
265	    ],
266	} }
267	{ "id": 10, "result": {
268	    "thread": {
269	        "id": "thr_123",
270	        "preview": "",
271	        "modelProvider": "openai",
272	        "createdAt": 1730910000
273	    }
274	} }
275	{ "method": "thread/started", "params": { "thread": { … } } }
276	```
277	
278	Valid `personality` values are `"friendly"`, `"pragmatic"`, and `"none"`. When `"none"` is selected, the personality placeholder is replaced with an empty string.
279	
280	To continue a stored session, call `thread/resume` with the `thread.id` you previously recorded. The response shape matches `thread/start`. When the stored session includes persisted token usage, the server emits `thread/tokenUsage/updated` immediately after the response so clients can render restored usage before the next turn starts. You can also pass the same configuration overrides supported by `thread/start`, including `approvalsReviewer`.
281	
282	By default, `thread/resume` includes the reconstructed turn history in `thread.turns`. Experimental clients can pass `excludeTurns: true` to return only thread metadata and live resume state, then call `thread/turns/list` separately if they want to page the turn history over the network. In that mode the server also skips replaying restored `thread/tokenUsage/updated`, which avoids rebuilding turns just to attribute historical usage.
283	
284	By default, resume uses the latest persisted `model` and `reasoningEffort` values associated with the thread. Supplying any of `model`, `modelProvider`, `config.model`, or `config.model_reasoning_effort` disables that persisted fallback and uses the explicit overrides plus normal config resolution instead.
285	
286	Example:
287	
288	```json
289	{ "method": "thread/resume", "id": 11, "params": {
290	    "threadId": "thr_123",
291	    "personality": "friendly"
292	} }
293	{ "id": 11, "result": { "thread": { "id": "thr_123", … } } }
294	
295	{ "method": "thread/resume", "id": 12, "params": {
296	    "threadId": "thr_123",
297	    "excludeTurns": true
298	} }
299	{ "id": 12, "result": { "thread": { "id": "thr_123", "turns": [], … } } }
300	```
301	
302	To branch from a stored session, call `thread/fork` with the `thread.id`. This creates a new thread id and emits a `thread/started` notification for it. The returned `thread.sessionId` identifies the current live session tree root. Root threads use their own `thread.id` as `thread.sessionId`; stored threads that are not loaded also report their own `thread.id`, because resuming one makes it the root of a new live session tree. When the source history includes persisted token usage, the server also emits `thread/tokenUsage/updated` for the new thread immediately after the response. If the source thread is actively running, the fork snapshots it as if the current turn had been interrupted first. Pass `ephemeral: true` when the fork should stay in-memory only:
303	
304	```json
305	{ "method": "thread/fork", "id": 12, "params": { "threadId": "thr_123", "ephemeral": true } }
306	{ "id": 12, "result": { "thread": { "id": "thr_456", "sessionId": "thr_456", … } } }
307	{ "method": "thread/started", "params": { "thread": { … } } }
308	```
309	
310	Like `thread/resume`, experimental clients can pass `excludeTurns: true` to `thread/fork` to return only thread metadata in `thread.turns` and page history with `thread/turns/list`. In that mode the server skips replaying restored `thread/tokenUsage/updated`, which keeps the fork path from rebuilding turns just to attribute historical usage.
311	
312	### Example: List threads (with pagination & filters)
313	
314	`thread/list` lets you render a history UI. Results default to `createdAt` (newest first) descending. Pass any combination of:
315	
316	- `cursor` — opaque string from a prior response; omit for the first page.
317	- `limit` — server defaults to a reasonable page size if unset.
318	- `sortKey` — `created_at` (default) or `updated_at`.
319	- `sortDirection` — `desc` (default) or `asc`.
320	- `modelProviders` — restrict results to specific providers; unset, null, or an empty array will include all providers.
321	- `sourceKinds` — restrict results to specific sources; omit or pass `[]` for interactive sessions only (`cli`, `vscode`).
322	- `archived` — when `true`, list archived threads only. When `false` or `null`, list non-archived threads (default).
323	- `cwd` — restrict results to threads whose session cwd exactly matches this path, or one of these paths when an array is provided. Relative paths are resolved against the app-server process cwd before matching.
324	- `useStateDbOnly` — when `true`, return from the state DB without scanning JSONL rollouts to repair metadata. Omit or pass `false` to preserve the default scan-and-repair behavior.
325	- `searchTerm` — restrict results to threads whose extracted title contains this substring (case-sensitive).
326	- Responses include `nextCursor` to continue in the same direction and `backwardsCursor` to pass as `cursor` when reversing `sortDirection`.
327	- Responses include `agentNickname` and `agentRole` for AgentControl-spawned thread sub-agents when available.
328	
329	Example:
330	
331	```json
332	{ "method": "thread/list", "id": 20, "params": {
333	    "cursor": null,
334	    "limit": 25,
335	    "cwd": ["/Users/me/project", "/Users/me/project-worktree"],
336	    "sortKey": "created_at"
337	} }
338	{ "id": 20, "result": {
339	    "data": [
340	        { "id": "thr_a", "preview": "Create a TUI", "modelProvider": "openai", "createdAt": 1730831111, "updatedAt": 1730831111, "status": { "type": "notLoaded" }, "agentNickname": "Atlas", "agentRole": "explorer" },
341	        { "id": "thr_b", "preview": "Fix tests", "modelProvider": "openai", "createdAt": 1730750000, "updatedAt": 1730750000, "status": { "type": "notLoaded" } }
342	    ],
343	    "nextCursor": "opaque-token-or-null",
344	    "backwardsCursor": "opaque-token-or-null"
345	} }
346	```
347	
348	When `nextCursor` is `null`, you’ve reached the final page.
349	
350	### Example: List loaded threads
351	
352	`thread/loaded/list` returns thread ids currently loaded in memory. This is useful when you want to check which sessions are active without scanning rollouts on disk.
353	
354	```json
355	{ "method": "thread/loaded/list", "id": 21 }
356	{ "id": 21, "result": {
357	    "data": ["thr_123", "thr_456"]
358	} }
359	```
360	
361	### Example: Track thread status changes
362	
363	`thread/status/changed` is emitted whenever a loaded thread's status changes after it has already been introduced to the client:
364	
365	- Includes `threadId` and the new `status`.
366	- Status can be `notLoaded`, `idle`, `systemError`, or `active` (with `activeFlags`; `active` implies running).
367	- `thread/start`, `thread/fork`, and detached review threads do not emit a separate initial `thread/status/changed`; their `thread/started` notification already carries the current `thread.status`.
368	
369	```json
370	{
371	  "method": "thread/status/changed",
372	  "params": {
373	    "threadId": "thr_123",
374	    "status": { "type": "active", "activeFlags": [] }
375	  }
376	}
377	```
378	
379	### Example: Unsubscribe from a loaded thread
380	
381	`thread/unsubscribe` removes the current connection's subscription to a thread. The response status is one of:
382	
383	- `unsubscribed` when the connection was subscribed and is now removed.
384	- `notSubscribed` when the connection was not subscribed to that thread.
385	- `notLoaded` when the thread is not loaded.
386	
387	If this was the last subscriber, the server does not unload the thread immediately. It unloads the thread after the thread has had no subscribers and no thread activity for 30 minutes, then emits `thread/closed` and a `thread/status/changed` transition to `notLoaded`.
388	
389	```json
390	{ "method": "thread/unsubscribe", "id": 22, "params": { "threadId": "thr_123" } }
391	{ "id": 22, "result": { "status": "unsubscribed" } }
392	```
393	
394	Later, after the idle unload timeout:
395	
396	```json
397	{ "method": "thread/status/changed", "params": {
398	    "threadId": "thr_123",
399	    "status": { "type": "notLoaded" }
400	} }
401	{ "method": "thread/closed", "params": { "threadId": "thr_123" } }
402	```
403	
404	### Example: Read a thread
405	
406	Use `thread/read` to fetch a stored thread by id without resuming it. Pass `includeTurns` when you want thread history loaded into `thread.turns`. The returned thread includes `agentNickname` and `agentRole` for AgentControl-spawned thread sub-agents when available.
407	
408	```json
409	{ "method": "thread/read", "id": 22, "params": { "threadId": "thr_123" } }
410	{ "id": 22, "result": {
411	    "thread": { "id": "thr_123", "status": { "type": "notLoaded" }, "turns": [] }
412	} }
413	```
414	
415	```json
416	{ "method": "thread/read", "id": 23, "params": { "threadId": "thr_123", "includeTurns": true } }
417	{ "id": 23, "result": {
418	    "thread": { "id": "thr_123", "status": { "type": "notLoaded" }, "turns": [ ... ] }
419	} }
420	```

422	### Example: List thread turns (experimental)
423	
424	Use `thread/turns/list` with `capabilities.experimentalApi = true` to page a stored thread’s turn history without resuming it. By default, results are sorted descending so clients can start at the present and fetch older turns with `nextCursor`. The response also includes `backwardsCursor`; pass it as `cursor` on a later request with `sortDirection: "asc"` to fetch turns newer than the first item from the earlier page.
425	
426	Every returned `Turn` includes `itemsView`, which tells clients whether the `items` array was omitted intentionally (`notLoaded`), contains only summary items (`summary`), or contains every item available from persisted app-server history (`full`). Pass `itemsView` to choose the returned detail level; omitted `itemsView` defaults to `"summary"`.
427	
428	```json
429	{ "method": "thread/turns/list", "id": 24, "params": {
430	    "threadId": "thr_123",
431	    "limit": 50,
432	    "sortDirection": "desc",
433	    "itemsView": "summary"
434	} }
435	{ "id": 24, "result": {
436	    "data": [ ... ],
437	    "nextCursor": "older-turns-cursor-or-null",
438	    "backwardsCursor": "newer-turns-cursor-or-null"
439	} }
440	```
441	
442	`thread/turns/items/list` is the planned hydration API for fetching full items for one turn:
443	
444	```json
445	{ "method": "thread/turns/items/list", "id": 25, "params": {
446	    "threadId": "thr_123",
447	    "turnId": "turn_456",
448	    "limit": 100,
449	    "sortDirection": "asc"
450	} }
451	```
452	
453	This method currently returns JSON-RPC `-32601` with message `thread/turns/items/list is not supported yet`.
454

500	### Example: Set and update a thread goal
501	
502	Use `thread/goal/set` to create or update the current goal for a materialized thread. Clients can set `budgetLimited` when they stop because a token budget is exhausted or nearly exhausted, `blocked` when progress is waiting on outside intervention, and `usageLimited` when usage availability stops further work. The system also sets `budgetLimited` when accounting crosses a configured token budget and `usageLimited` when a turn ends on a hard usage-limit error.
503	
504	```json
505	{ "method": "thread/goal/set", "id": 27, "params": {
506	    "threadId": "thr_123",
507	    "objective": "Keep improving the benchmark until p95 latency is under 120ms",
508	    "tokenBudget": 200000
509	} }
510	{ "id": 27, "result": { "goal": {
511	    "threadId": "thr_123",
512	    "objective": "Keep improving the benchmark until p95 latency is under 120ms",
513	    "status": "active",
514	    "tokenBudget": 200000,
515	    "tokensUsed": 0,
516	    "timeUsedSeconds": 0,
517	    "createdAt": 1776272400,
518	    "updatedAt": 1776272400
519	} } }
520	{ "method": "thread/goal/updated", "params": { "threadId": "thr_123", "goal": {
521	    "threadId": "thr_123",
522	    "objective": "Keep improving the benchmark until p95 latency is under 120ms",
523	    "status": "active",
524	    "tokenBudget": 200000,
525	    "tokensUsed": 0,
526	    "timeUsedSeconds": 0,
527	    "createdAt": 1776272400,
528	    "updatedAt": 1776272400
529	} } }
530	```

532	```json
533	{ "method": "thread/goal/set", "id": 28, "params": {
534	    "threadId": "thr_123",
535	    "status": "blocked"
536	} }

538	    "threadId": "thr_123",
539	    "objective": "Keep improving the benchmark until p95 latency is under 120ms",
540	    "status": "blocked",

586	### Example: Trigger thread compaction
587	
588	Use `thread/compact/start` to trigger manual history compaction for a thread. The request returns immediately with `{}`.
589	
590	Progress is emitted as standard `turn/*` and `item/*` notifications on the same `threadId`. Clients should expect a single compaction item:
591	
592	- `item/started` with `item: { "type": "contextCompaction", ... }`
593	- `item/completed` with the same `contextCompaction` item id
594	
595	While compaction is running, the thread is effectively in a turn so clients should surface progress UI based on the notifications.
596	
597	```json
598	{ "method": "thread/compact/start", "id": 25, "params": { "threadId": "thr_b" } }
599	{ "id": 25, "result": {} }
600	```

602	### Example: Run a thread shell command
603	
604	Use `thread/shellCommand` for the TUI `!` workflow. The request returns immediately with `{}`.
605	This API runs unsandboxed with full access; it does not inherit the thread
606	sandbox policy.
607	
608	If the thread already has an active turn, the command runs as an auxiliary action on that turn. In that case, progress is emitted as standard `item/*` notifications on the existing turn and the formatted output is injected into the turn’s message stream:
609	
610	- `item/started` with `item: { "type": "commandExecution", "source": "userShell", ... }`
611	- zero or more `item/commandExecution/outputDelta`
612	- `item/completed` with the same `commandExecution` item id
613	
614	If the thread does not already have an active turn, the server starts a standalone turn for the shell command. In that case clients should expect:
615	
616	- `turn/started`
617	- `item/started` with `item: { "type": "commandExecution", "source": "userShell", ... }`
618	- zero or more `item/commandExecution/outputDelta`
619	- `item/completed` with the same `commandExecution` item id
620	- `turn/completed`
621	
622	```json
623	{ "method": "thread/shellCommand", "id": 26, "params": { "threadId": "thr_b", "command": "git status --short" } }
624	{ "id": 26, "result": {} }
625	```
626	
627	### Example: Start a turn (send user input)
628	
629	Turns attach user input (text or images) to a thread and trigger Codex generation. The `input` field is a list of discriminated unions:
630	
631	- `{"type":"text","text":"Explain this diff"}`
632	- `{"type":"image","url":"https://…png"}`
633	- `{"type":"localImage","path":"/tmp/screenshot.png"}`
634	
635	You can optionally specify config overrides on the new turn. If specified, these settings become the default for subsequent turns on the same thread. `outputSchema` applies only to the current turn. Experimental `environments` is turn-scoped: omit it to inherit the thread's sticky environments, pass `[]` to run the turn with no environments, or pass explicit environment ids to override the sticky selection for this turn only.
636	
637	`approvalsReviewer` accepts:
638	
639	- `"user"` — default. Review approval requests directly in the client.
640	- `"auto_review"` — route approval requests to a carefully prompted subagent, which gathers relevant context and applies a risk-based decision framework before approving or denying the request. The legacy value `"guardian_subagent"` is still accepted for compatibility.
641	
642	```json
643	{ "method": "turn/start", "id": 30, "params": {
644	    "threadId": "thr_123",
645	    "input": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Run tests" } ],
646	    // Below are optional config overrides
647	    "cwd": "/Users/me/project",
648	    // Experimental: turn-scoped environment selection.
649	    "environments": [
650	        { "environmentId": "local", "cwd": "/Users/me/project" }
651	    ],
652	    "approvalPolicy": "unlessTrusted",
653	    "sandboxPolicy": {
654	        "type": "workspaceWrite",
655	        "writableRoots": ["/Users/me/project"],
656	        "networkAccess": true
657	    },
658	    // Prefer experimental profile selection:
659	    // "permissions": ":workspace"
660	    // Experimental runtime roots for :workspace_roots materialization:
661	    // "runtimeWorkspaceRoots": ["/Users/me/project", "/Users/me/openai"],
662	    // Do not send both "sandboxPolicy" and "permissions".
663	    "model": "gpt-5.1-codex",
664	    "effort": "medium",
665	    "summary": "concise",
666	    "personality": "friendly",
667	    // Optional JSON Schema to constrain the final assistant message for this turn.
668	    "outputSchema": {
669	        "type": "object",
670	        "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string" } },
671	        "required": ["answer"],
672	        "additionalProperties": false
673	    }
674	} }
675	{ "id": 30, "result": { "turn": {
676	    "id": "turn_456",
677	    "status": "inProgress",
678	    "items": [],
679	    "error": null
680	} } }
681	```

761	### Example: Start realtime with WebRTC
762	
763	Use `thread/realtime/start` with `transport.type: "webrtc"` when a browser or webview owns the `RTCPeerConnection` and app-server should create the server-side realtime session. The transport `sdp` must be the offer SDP produced by `RTCPeerConnection.createOffer()`, not a hand-written or minimal SDP string.
764	
765	The offer should include the media sections the client wants to negotiate. For the standard realtime UI flow, create the audio track/transceiver and the `oai-events` data channel before calling `createOffer()`:
766	
767	```javascript
768	const pc = new RTCPeerConnection();
769	
770	audioElement.autoplay = true;
771	pc.ontrack = (event) => {
772	  audioElement.srcObject = event.streams[0];
773	};
774	
775	const mediaStream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true });
776	pc.addTrack(mediaStream.getAudioTracks()[0], mediaStream);
777	pc.createDataChannel("oai-events");
778	
779	const offer = await pc.createOffer();
780	await pc.setLocalDescription(offer);
781	```
782	
783	Then send `offer.sdp` to app-server. Core uses `experimental_realtime_ws_backend_prompt` for the backend instructions and the thread conversation id as the default Realtime API session identifier. This `realtimeSessionId` value refers to the upstream Realtime API session, not a Codex session/thread-group id. The start response is `{}`; the remote answer SDP arrives later as `thread/realtime/sdp` and should be passed to `setRemoteDescription()`:
784	
785	```json
786	{ "method": "thread/realtime/start", "id": 40, "params": {
787	    "threadId": "thr_123",
788	    "outputModality": "audio",
789	    "prompt": "You are on a call.",
790	    "realtimeSessionId": null,
791	    "transport": { "type": "webrtc", "sdp": "v=0\r\no=..." }
792	} }
793	{ "id": 40, "result": {} }
794	{ "method": "thread/realtime/sdp", "params": {
795	    "threadId": "thr_123",
796	    "sdp": "v=0\r\no=..."
797	} }
798	```
799	
800	Omit `prompt` to use Codex's default realtime backend prompt. Send `prompt: null` or
801	`prompt: ""` when the session should start without that default backend prompt.
802	
803	```javascript
804	await pc.setRemoteDescription({
805	  type: "answer",
806	  sdp: notification.params.sdp,
807	});
808	```

810	### Example: Interrupt an active turn
811	
812	You can cancel a running Turn with `turn/interrupt`.
813	
814	```json
815	{ "method": "turn/interrupt", "id": 31, "params": {
816	    "threadId": "thr_123",
817	    "turnId": "turn_456"
818	} }
819	{ "id": 31, "result": {} }
820	```
821	
822	The server requests cancellation of the active turn, then emits a `turn/completed` event with `status: "interrupted"`. This does not terminate background terminals; use `thread/backgroundTerminals/clean` when you explicitly want to stop those shells. Rely on the `turn/completed` event to know when turn interruption has finished.

835	### Example: Steer an active turn
836	
837	Use `turn/steer` to append additional user input to the currently active regular turn. This does
838	not emit `turn/started` and does not accept thread settings overrides.
839	
840	```json
841	{ "method": "turn/steer", "id": 32, "params": {
842	    "threadId": "thr_123",
843	    "input": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Actually focus on failing tests first." } ],
844	    "expectedTurnId": "turn_456"
845	} }
846	{ "id": 32, "result": { "turnId": "turn_456" } }
847	```
848	
849	`expectedTurnId` is required. If there is no active turn, `expectedTurnId` does not match the
850	active turn, or the active turn kind does not accept same-turn steering (for example review or
851	manual compaction), the request fails with an `invalid request` error.

853	### Example: Request a code review
854	
855	Use `review/start` to run Codex’s reviewer on the currently checked-out project. The request takes the thread id plus a `target` describing what should be reviewed:
856	
857	- `{"type":"uncommittedChanges"}` — staged, unstaged, and untracked files.
858	- `{"type":"baseBranch","branch":"main"}` — diff against the provided branch’s upstream (see prompt for the exact `git merge-base`/`git diff` instructions Codex will run).
859	- `{"type":"commit","sha":"abc1234","title":"Optional subject"}` — review a specific commit.
860	- `{"type":"custom","instructions":"Free-form reviewer instructions"}` — fallback prompt equivalent to the legacy manual review request.
861	- `delivery` (`"inline"` or `"detached"`, default `"inline"`) — where the review runs:
862	  - `"inline"`: run the review as a new turn on the existing thread. The response’s `reviewThreadId` equals the original `threadId`, and no new `thread/started` notification is emitted.
863	  - `"detached"`: fork a new review thread from the parent conversation and run the review there. The response’s `reviewThreadId` is the id of this new review thread, and the server emits a `thread/started` notification for it before streaming review items.
864	
865	Example request/response:
866	
867	```json
868	{ "method": "review/start", "id": 40, "params": {
869	    "threadId": "thr_123",
870	    "delivery": "inline",
871	    "target": { "type": "commit", "sha": "1234567deadbeef", "title": "Polish tui colors" }
872	} }
873	{ "id": 40, "result": {
874	    "turn": {
875	        "id": "turn_900",
876	        "status": "inProgress",
877	        "items": [
878	            { "type": "userMessage", "id": "turn_900", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Review commit 1234567: Polish tui colors" } ] }
879	        ],
880	        "error": null
881	    },
882	    "reviewThreadId": "thr_123"
883	} }
884	```
885	
886	For a detached review, use `"delivery": "detached"`. The response is the same shape, but `reviewThreadId` will be the id of the new review thread (different from the original `threadId`). The server also emits a `thread/started` notification for that new thread before streaming the review turn.
887	
888	Codex streams the usual `turn/started` notification followed by an `item/started`
889	with an `enteredReviewMode` item so clients can show progress:
890	
891	```json
892	{
893	  "method": "item/started",
894	  "params": {
895	    "item": {
896	      "type": "enteredReviewMode",
897	      "id": "turn_900",
898	      "review": "current changes"
899	    }
900	  }
901	}
902	```
903	
904	When the reviewer finishes, the server emits `item/started` and `item/completed`
905	containing an `exitedReviewMode` item with the final review text:
906	
907	```json
908	{
909	  "method": "item/completed",
910	  "params": {
911	    "item": {
912	      "type": "exitedReviewMode",
913	      "id": "turn_900",
914	      "review": "Looks solid overall...\n\n- Prefer Stylize helpers — app.rs:10-20\n  ..."
915	    }
916	  }
917	}
918	```
919	
920	The `review` string is plain text that already bundles the overall explanation plus a bullet list for each structured finding (matching `ThreadItem::ExitedReviewMode` in the generated schema). Use this notification to render the reviewer output in your client.
921	
922	### Example: One-off command execution
923	
924	Run a standalone command (argv vector) in the server’s sandbox without creating a thread or turn:
925	
926	```json
927	{ "method": "command/exec", "id": 32, "params": {
928	    "command": ["ls", "-la"],
929	    "processId": "ls-1",                           // optional string; required for streaming and ability to terminate the process
930	    "cwd": "/Users/me/project",                    // optional; defaults to server cwd
931	    "env": { "FOO": "override" },                  // optional; merges into the server env and overrides matching names
932	    "size": { "rows": 40, "cols": 120 },           // optional; PTY size in character cells, only valid with tty=true
933	    "permissionProfile": ":workspace",             // optional profile id; defaults to user config
934	    "outputBytesCap": 1048576,                     // optional; per-stream capture cap
935	    "disableOutputCap": false,                     // optional; cannot be combined with outputBytesCap
936	    "timeoutMs": 10000,                            // optional; ms timeout; defaults to server timeout
937	    "disableTimeout": false                        // optional; cannot be combined with timeoutMs
938	} }
939	{ "id": 32, "result": {
940	    "exitCode": 0,
941	    "stdout": "...",
942	    "stderr": ""
943	} }
944	```
945	
946	- Prefer using `process/spawn` when you want an explicitly unsandboxed process execution API with immediate spawn acknowledgement, handle-based control, output notifications, and an exit notification.
947	- For clients that are already sandboxed externally, set the legacy `sandboxPolicy` to `{"type":"externalSandbox","networkAccess":"enabled"}` (or omit `networkAccess` to keep it restricted). Codex will not enforce its own sandbox in this mode; it tells the model it has full file-system access and passes the `networkAccess` state through `environment_context`.
948	
949	Notes:
950	
951	- Empty `command` arrays are rejected.
952	- Prefer `permissionProfile` for command permission overrides. It selects an active profile by id (for example `:read-only`, `:workspace`, or a user-defined `[permissions.<id>]` profile) rather than accepting low-level filesystem/network permissions. The legacy `sandboxPolicy` field accepts the same shape used by `turn/start` (e.g., `dangerFullAccess`, `readOnly`, `workspaceWrite` with flags, `externalSandbox` with `networkAccess` `restricted|enabled`), but cannot be combined with `permissionProfile`.
953	- `env` merges into the environment produced by the server's shell environment policy. Matching names are overridden; unspecified variables are left intact.
954	- When omitted, `timeoutMs` falls back to the server default.
955	- When omitted, `outputBytesCap` falls back to the server default of 1 MiB per stream.
956	- `disableOutputCap: true` disables stdout/stderr capture truncation for that `command/exec` request. It cannot be combined with `outputBytesCap`.
957	- `disableTimeout: true` disables the timeout entirely for that `command/exec` request. It cannot be combined with `timeoutMs`.
958	- `processId` is optional for buffered execution. When omitted, Codex generates an internal id for lifecycle tracking, but `tty`, `streamStdin`, and `streamStdoutStderr` must stay disabled and follow-up `command/exec/write` / `command/exec/terminate` calls are not available for that command.
959	- `size` is only valid when `tty: true`. It sets the initial PTY size in character cells.
960	- Buffered Windows sandbox execution accepts `processId` for correlation, but `command/exec/write` and `command/exec/terminate` are still unsupported for those requests.
961	- Buffered Windows sandbox execution also requires the default output cap; custom `outputBytesCap` and `disableOutputCap` are unsupported there.
962	- `tty`, `streamStdin`, and `streamStdoutStderr` are optional booleans. Legacy requests that omit them continue to use buffered execution.
963	- `tty: true` implies PTY mode plus `streamStdin: true` and `streamStdoutStderr: true`.
964	- `tty` and `streamStdin` do not disable the timeout on their own; omit `timeoutMs` to use the server default timeout, or set `disableTimeout: true` to keep the process alive until exit or explicit termination.
965	- `outputBytesCap` applies independently to `stdout` and `stderr`, and streamed bytes are not duplicated into the final response.
966	- The `command/exec` response is deferred until the process exits and is sent only after all `command/exec/outputDelta` notifications for that connection have been emitted.
967	- `command/exec/outputDelta` notifications are connection-scoped. If the originating connection closes, the server terminates the process.
968	
969	Streaming stdin/stdout uses base64 so PTY sessions can carry arbitrary bytes:
970	
971	```json
972	{ "method": "command/exec", "id": 33, "params": {
973	    "command": ["bash", "-i"],
974	    "processId": "bash-1",
975	    "tty": true,
976	    "outputBytesCap": 32768
977	} }
978	{ "method": "command/exec/outputDelta", "params": {
979	    "processId": "bash-1",
980	    "stream": "stdout",
981	    "deltaBase64": "YmFzaC00LjQkIA==",
982	    "capReached": false

Now let me create a comprehensive findings summary. I have enough information to map the relay architecture thoroughly.

## FINDINGS: CODEX DOCK RELAY ARCHITECTURE

### 1. CLIENT-FACING HTTP/WebSocket ENDPOINTS

The relay exposes **JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket** to downstream Swift clients. Main methods:

**HTTP REST Endpoints** (`dock-relay.mjs:627-671`):
- `GET /readyz` – readiness probe (always 200)
- `GET /healthz` – health check including auth mode and transcription config
- `GET /statusz` – full status snapshot (calls `checkRawAppServerHealth` first)
- `GET /metricsz` – request metrics by method (loopback-only)
- `GET /debugz/sessions` – active session debug info (loopback-only)

**JSON-RPC Methods** (`dock-relay.mjs:450-491`):
| Method | Handler | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `initialize` | returns userAgent, codexHome, platformFamily, relayInstanceID | Setup handshake |
| `thread/list` | `aggregateThreadList()` | History + live overlay + summaries |
| `thread/loaded/list` | `aggregateLoadedList()` | Live thread IDs only |
| `thread/read` | `aggregateThreadRead()` | Route to live or history |
| `thread/turns/list` | `listThreadTurns()` | Route to live or history |
| `thread/resume` | `resumeThread()` | Open live upstream WebSocket session |
| `thread/archive` | `archiveThread()` | Route to live or history |
| `thread/unarchive` | `unarchiveThread()` | History only |
| `audio/transcription/start`, `append`, `commit`, `cancel` | `RealtimeTranscriptionManager` | OpenAI realtime transcription proxy |
| `turn/start`, `turn/steer`, `turn/interrupt` | `forwardToActiveUpstream()` | Forwarded to active thread's upstream |

---

### 2. UPSTREAM CALLS (TO APP-SERVER)

The relay makes **JSON-RPC requests** to two upstream sources:

**History App-Server** (`dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:425-541`):
- URL: `config.historyUrl` (default `ws://127.0.0.1:4500`)
- Requests: `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/archive`, `thread/unarchive`
- Bearer token: `config.historyBearerToken` (required)
- Pooled with label `"history"` (max 1 open connection)

**Live App-Servers** (loopback discovery, `dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:211-227`):
- Discovery: `ps` regex match on `codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:<port>`
- Request: `thread/loaded/list` + `thread/read` (no turns) per endpoint
- Each endpoint gets bearerToken (typically same as history)
- Pooled with label `"live-status"` (max 4 concurrent per endpoint)

**Live Upstream (per-session)** (`dock-relay.mjs:313-338`, session-focused):
- Called after `thread/resume` opens a session
- Methods: `thread/resume`, `thread/turns/list`, then `turn/start`, `turn/steer`, `turn/interrupt`
- Uses separate per-session client (not pooled)
- Forwards server-initiated `onRequest` (live requests) and `onNotification` to downstream

---

### 3. CACHING LAYERS

#### **Live Status Cache** (`dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs`)
- **What**: Cached discovery results: endpoints, thread rows, endpoint health
- **Where**: `config.liveStatusCache` (in-memory)
- **Key**: N/A (single global snapshot)
- **TTL/Refresh**:
  - Refresh interval: `LIVE_STATUS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 2500ms` (lines 27, 53)
  - Max age for routing: `LIVE_STATUS_MAX_AGE_MS = 5000ms` (lines 26, 144-148)
  - Auto-refresh started on `start()` (line 74), fires async every 2.5s
  - If snapshot older than 5s, `snapshotForRouting()` triggers fresh refresh (line 145)
- **Warming**: `collectLiveRows()` called periodically; uses pool concurrency `"live-status"` label (max 4)
- **State**:
  - `checkedAt` (ISO timestamp), `checkedAtMs` (Date.now())
  - `endpoints[]`, `failedEndpoints` count
  - `rows[]` (merged thread data with `dockRelaySource` endpoint attached)
  - `ok`, `status`, `error`
- **Failure Handling**:
  - Individual endpoint failures caught; count tracked as `failedEndpoints`
  - Overlay state: "ready" (all ok), "degraded" (some failed), "stale" (older than 5s), "unavailable" / "disabled"
  - If overall collection fails, `ok=false`, `status="down"` recorded (lines 117-133)

#### **Thread Summary Cache** (`dock-relay-thread-summary-cache.mjs`)
- **What**: Latest text summary extracted from most recent userMessage/agentMessage in thread
- **Where**: `config.threadSummaryCache` (in-memory Map)
- **Key**: threadId (deduplicated, max 500 entries, LRU eviction)
- **TTL/Refresh**:

183	# 1) Key Design Considerations (what matters most)
184	
185	## 1.1 Priorities (ranked)
186	
187	1. Correct mental model: one relay host equals one endpoint.
188	2. Real deletion: remove endpoint arrays, alias merging, and fallback loops instead of hiding them.
189	3. Fail-loud behavior: if a configured host is down, that host is offline.
190	4. Minimal config: phone-side host config requires only host and port.
191	5. Existing path fit: keep the current `HostRegistry`, `DockRelayEndpoint`, Makefile, and device-config ownership boundaries where they still make sense.
192	
193	## 1.2 Constraints
194	
195	- `.env` remains user-owned and must not be rewritten.
196	- Phone config must not receive `OPENAI_API_KEY`, raw app-server bearer tokens, or raw `:4500` endpoints.
197	- The app-facing relay remains `:4510`.
198	- `project.yml` changes are not expected unless implementation changes target settings, permissions, Info.plist, or assets.
199	- Physical phone proof must use Makefile-owned install/config targets, not raw platform install commands.
200	- Existing dirty worktree changes outside this plan are user-owned and must not be reverted.
201	
202	## 1.3 Architectural principles (rules we will enforce)
203	
204	- The Swift type should make the bad state impossible: a `DockHostConfiguration` cannot hold more than one endpoint.
205	- The registry owns host lists; individual hosts do not own endpoint lists.
206	- The connector owns a single connection attempt to a host endpoint. Reconnect policy may still exist inside live detail transport, but not as same-host endpoint fallback.
207	- Device config writer and reader use the same simple host-list contract.
208	- Relay identity is observation, not configuration grouping.
209	- Tests should assert behavior and contracts, not absence of strings or doc inventory.
210	
211	## 1.4 Known tradeoffs (explicit)
212	
213	- Old saved multi-endpoint JSON will stop loading. That is intentional because this is a clean cutover.
214	- If `Amir-M5.local:4510` fails, the app will mark that host offline instead of silently trying `192.168.50.74:4510` as an alias. The user should see which host route failed.
215	- Display names may initially be endpoint-derived until a relay response provides richer metadata. The implementation must not use that metadata to merge rows.
216	- Keeping `CODEX_DOCK_HOSTS` as a comma-separated list is acceptable because it represents a host list, not a per-host endpoint list.

61	    public static func redacted(_ value: String, maxLength: Int = 240) -> String {
62	        var result = value
63	        let replacements: [(String, String)] = [
64	            (#"(?i)bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]+"#, "Bearer <redacted>"),
65	            (#"(?i)(authorization|api[_-]?key|openai[_-]?api[_-]?key|token|secret)\s*[:=]\s*[^ \r\n;,]+"#, "$1=<redacted>"),
66	            (#"sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}"#, "sk-<redacted>"),
67	            (#"\b[A-Za-z0-9+/]{120,}={0,2}\b"#, "<redacted-large-token>"),
68	        ]
69	
70	        for (pattern, template) in replacements {
71	            guard let regex = try? NSRegularExpression(pattern: pattern) else {
72	                continue
73	            }
74	            let range = NSRange(result.startIndex..<result.endIndex, in: result)
75	            result = regex.stringByReplacingMatches(
76	                in: result,
77	                range: range,
78	                withTemplate: template
79	            )
80	        }
81	
82	        return clipped(result, maxLength: maxLength)
83	    }

86	        guard value.count > maxLength else {
87	            return value
88	        }
89	        let suffix = "..."
90	        let endIndex = value.index(value.startIndex, offsetBy: max(0, maxLength - suffix.count))
91	        return "\(value[..<endIndex])\(suffix)"
92	    }

13	# Working Draft
14	
15	This document is the on-disk workspace for the model-consensus architecture pass. It intentionally starts as a target-architecture shell, not as a preservation plan for the current implementation.
16	
17	The final version should answer one question:
18	
19	```text
20	What architecture makes Codex Dock fast, stable, resilient, provider-agnostic, and simple on the client?
21	```
22	
23	# Raw Goal
24	
25	Design the perfect architecture for Codex Dock where the relay does the hard work and the client receives a clean, simple, robust protocol. The architecture should support full updates, incremental updates, resync, transient failure tolerance, fast startup, provider abstraction, and future non-Codex providers such as Claude Code without requiring client rewrites.
26	
27	Do not implement anything in this pass.
28	
29	# Non-Negotiables
30	
31	- The relay is the aggregator and durability boundary for Dock state.
32	- The client does not decode raw Codex app-server details.
33	- The client does not stitch together history, live state, cursors, and failure recovery.
34	- The client can render from one clean over-the-wire model.
35	- The relay supports full snapshot, incremental updates, and explicit resync.
36	- Slow or failing upstream providers never erase last-known-good client state.
37	- Runtime/provider weirdness is isolated behind relay-side adapters.
38	- Secrets stay relay-side.
39	- The design does not preserve current architecture for its own sake.
40	- The design avoids feature sprawl.
41	
42	# Consensus Workspace
43	
44	The model pass should fill in:
45	
46	- architecture thesis
47	- component boundaries
48	- relay state model
49	- provider adapter contract
50	- wire protocol
51	- update and resync semantics
52	- failure and staleness semantics
53	- security model
54	- client model
55	- migration plan
56	- test strategy
57	- rejected alternatives
58	- open decisions
59	
60	# Audit Notes
61	
62	The parent agent will audit model output against:
63	
64	- whether the client is actually simple
65	- whether the relay owns aggregation instead of forwarding raw complexity
66	- whether the protocol is provider-agnostic
67	- whether slow Home-like refreshes remain visually stable
68	- whether `notLoaded`-style provider internals are hidden or normalized
69	- whether the design supports full snapshot, incremental update, and resync
70	- whether the design is resilient without becoming a kitchen sink

Perfect. Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me compile my findings:

## STRUCTURED FINDINGS: CODEX DOCK CLIENT ARCHITECTURE MAPPING

Based on my thorough analysis of the Swift client codebase, here is what I found:

---

### 1. CODEX-SPECIFIC DECODING IN THE CLIENT

The client is **deeply coupled** to Codex's domain model. The decoding logic spans multiple files:

**ThreadSourceKind enum** (AppServer/ThreadListDTO.swift:50-71):
- Enumerates 9 sourceKind variants:
  - `.cli`, `.vscode` (human origins)
  - `.exec`, `.appServer`, `.subAgentReview`, `.subAgentCompact`, `.subAgentThreadSpawn`, `.subAgentOther` (agent/automation origins)
  - `.unknown`
- Includes hardcoded `dockAgentScopeKinds` list (line 62-70) that groups automation sources for agent-scope queries

**ThreadStatusDTO enum** (ThreadListDTO.swift:256-306):
- Custom Codable implementation decoding `type` field into:
  - `.notLoaded`, `.idle`, `.systemError`
  - `.active(activeFlags: [ThreadActiveFlagDTO])`
  - `.unknown(String)`
- Maps to SessionStatus in the client (SessionSummaryMapper.swift:328-345)

**SessionSummaryMapper decoding logic** (Models/SessionSummaryMapper.swift:148-191):
- Classifies thread origin via complex `classifySource(_:)` matching (line 227-277):
  - Looks for keys like "subAgent", "subagent", nested "source" objects
  - Checks object keys and "type", "kind", "sourceKind", "source_kind", "subtype" fields
  - Recursively traverses nested JSON to find recognized signals
- Maps human CLI/VSCode identifiers to `SessionHumanOriginSubtype` (line 282-287)
- Maps exec, appServer, subAgent* identifiers to `SessionAgentOriginSubtype` (line 290-300)
- Falls back to `.unknown` origin when evidence contradicts source signals (line 168-179)

**SessionOrigin enum** (Models/SessionSummary.swift:83-167):
- Wraps classified origin with evidence bag: `sourceKind`, `rawSource`, `threadSource`, `agentNickname`, `agentRole`
- Discriminates three cases: `.human(subtype, evidence)`, `.automation(subtype, evidence)`, `.unknownOrigin(evidence)`

**ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO** (ThreadListDTO.swift:116-148):
- Carries relay health status: `ok` (Bool), `state` (String?), `ageMs` (Int?)
- Client extracts `degradedMessage` from `state` values: "disabled", "unavailable", "stale", etc. (line 135-147)

---

### 2. MULTI-STREAM MERGING IN THE CLIENT

DockStore performs **fan-out load and multi-scope merging** (State/DockStore.swift):

**Merge structure** (lines 624-663):
- `HostLoadOutcome` bundles per-host results from two scopes (`DockSessionScope.human`, `.agents`)
- Each scope has its own `Result<DockLoadResult, DockLoadFailure>` (line 626)
- `completeFailure` property returns the scope error only if **both** scopes fail (line 643-662)

**Snapshot building** (lines 746-837):
- Iterates over `HostLoadOutcome` results
- Extracts successful summaries per scope via `successfulScopedSummaries(from:)` (lines 839-851) and wraps in `ScopedSessionSummary(scope, summary)` tuples
- Deduplicates via `deduplicated(summaries)` (lines 876-919):
  - Groups summaries by `HostScopedThreadID` (line 877)
  - Tracks which scopes contributed to each thread (line 879)
  - If a thread appears in both scopes, creates a `DockScopeConflictViewModel` (line 900-905)
  - Uses `shouldPrefer(candidate, over: existing)` to pick the "winning" summary when duplicates exist (line 910-912):
    - Prefers human over agent if both exist
    - Prefers agent over unknown
- **Extracts liveOverlay messages** via `successfulLiveOverlayMessages(from:)` (lines 853-864):
  - Collects `liveOverlay.degradedMessage` from all scopes
  - Combines into partial-status message (line 789, 801-803)

**Host state rollup** (lines 766-812):
- Per-host status becomes:
  - `.offline(message)` or `.error(message)` if **all** scopes failed (completeFailure check, line 778-784)
  - `.partial(rowCount, message)` if scopes have individual failures or liveOverlay degradation (line 785-803)
  - `.loaded(rowCount)` or `.empty` if all succeeded with no overlay issues (line 805-811)

**Paging & cursor state** (AppServerDockClient.swift:101-157):
- Loops over `maxPages` (hardcoded to 1 in CodexDockConstants.Dock.activeSessionMaxPages, line 19)
- Accumulates cursor-paginated results in a single `summaries` array (line 108)
- Tracks cursor position and guards against infinite loops via `seenCursors` set (line 145-146)
- Combines backward and forward cursors (line 131-132) but doesn't use them in the current scope context

---

### 3. FAILURE & RECOVERY LOGIC IN THE CLIENT

**Partial snapshots without stale-while-refresh** (DockStore.swift:603-622):
- `loadAllHostsPublishingPartial()` publishes **intermediate snapshots while hosts are still checking** (line 665-691):
  - Maintains `checkingHostIDs` set to track incomplete hosts (line 675)
  - For each completed host, updates state with `makeSnapshot(results: outcomes, checkingHostIDs: checkingHostIDs)` (line 683)
  - Sets `isPartial: true` in snapshot if any hosts are still loading (line 835)
- **No stale-while-refresh logic**: if a host errors partway through, partial data is returned but with error status, not cached data

**Scope-level error handling**:
- `loadScope()` (line 721-737) wraps exceptions in `DockLoadFailure.error(message)` for 9 app-server error types:
  - `.duplicateRequestID`, `.malformedMessage`, `.requestCancelled`, `.responseDecoding`, `.server`, `.unexpectedServerRequest`, `.unmatchedResponse` → `.error(...)`
  - `.disconnected`, `.notConnected`, `.requestTimedOut`, `.transport` → `.offline(...)`
- Maps into scope-level failures only; host remains in `.partial` state (line 785-794)

**No explicit retry at Dock level**:
- `refresh()` calls `reload(showLoading: false)` which re-fans to all hosts and scopes each time (line 531-532)
- Relies on AppServerClient's reconnect policy for connection recovery; no retry loop at Dock level

**AppServerClient reconnect policy** (AppServerClient.swift:615-650):
- `connectionPolicy: AppServerConnectionPolicy` can have optional `AppServerReconnectPolicy` (line 34-40)
- Reconnect loop runs with exponential backoff up to `maxAttempts` (line 634)
- Respects `foregroundWorkGate` to pause reconnects when backgrounded (line 638)
- Fires reconnect only if policy exists and `initializeParams` were set (line 627-630)

---

### 4. REFRESH MODEL & AUTO-REFRESH

**load() vs refresh()**:
- `load()` calls `reload(showLoading: true)` → shows `.loading` state (line 527-528)
- `refresh()` calls `reload(showLoading: false)` → updates in-place without loading indicator (line 531-532)

**Paging parameters**:
- `DockSessionQuery` hardcodes `maxPages: CodexDockConstants.Dock.activeSessionMaxPages = 1` for both human and agent scopes (line 19, 43, 49)
- Page limit (250 rows) applied per scope via `pageLimit(for:)` (line 160-162):
  - Agents: `CodexDockConstants.Dock.agentSessionPageLimit = 250`
  - Humans: `CodexDockConstants.Dock.humanSessionPageLimit = 250`
- No auto-refresh loop in DockStore; relies on external lifecycle coordinator to call `refresh()` periodically

**Auto-refresh interval**:
- `DockStore.defaultAutoRefreshInterval: Duration = .seconds(5)` (line 447, CodexDockConstants.Dock.autoRefreshInterval)
- Not used internally; must be invoked by view controller or lifecycle handler

---

### 5. CLIENT DATA MODEL

**SessionSummary** (Models/SessionSummary.swift:169-208):
- Fields: `id` (HostScopedThreadID), `backendSessionID`, `displayTitle`, `status` (SessionStatus), `repository` (SessionSummaryText), `workingDirectory`, `branch`, `lastActivity` (Date), `shortEventSummary`, `origin` (SessionOrigin)
- `SessionStatus`: `.unknown`, `.notLoaded`, `.idle`, `.systemError`, `.active(activeFlags)`
- `SessionOrigin`: wraps classified origin + evidence

**DockRowViewModel** (DockStore.swift:165-188):
- UI-facing projection: `id`, `backendSessionID`, `title`, `hostDisplayName`, `hostEndpoint`, `repository`, `branch`, `status` (DockRowStatusKind: running/idle/notLoaded/error/unknown), `lastActivity` (Date + relative text), `summary`, `rail` (color), `label`, `origin`
- Built by SessionRowProjector (State/SessionRowProjector.swift:3-127) which applies local metadata (rail, label) and formats timestamps

**DockSnapshot** (DockStore.swift:290-323):
- Contains: primary `host`, all `hosts`, `hostStates` (per-host load status), rows, scope load failures, scope conflicts, mapping failures, `isPartial` flag
- Immutable snapshot captures a moment in the merge

---

### 6. CLIENT-TO-RELAY COMMUNICATION

**Transport**: WebSocket over HTTP(S) (AppServerClient.swift:878-965):
- `URLSessionWebSocketAppServerTransport` wraps URLSessionWebSocketTask (line 886)
- URL constructed from `DockRelayEndpoint.webSocketURL` (DockHostConfiguration.swift:17-19): `ws://host:port/`
- Bearer token passed as "Authorization: Bearer ..." header if present (line 902-903)
- Maximum message size: `CodexDockConstants.AppServer.maximumMessageSize = 512 * 1024 * 1024` (line 13)

**JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol** (AppServer/JSONRPC.swift):
- Requests: `JSONRPCRequest(id, method, params)` encoded as JSON text (line 501-502)
- Responses: `JSONRPCResponse(id, result)` or `JSONRPCErrorObject(code, message)`
- Notifications: `JSONRPCNotification(method, params)` (no id)

**Method calls**:
- `thread/list` (AppServerClient.swift:270-280): params = `ThreadListParams` (cursor, limit, sortKey, sortDirection, modelProviders=[], sourceKinds, archived)
- `thread/archive`, `thread/unarchive` (line 318-340): params = `ThreadArchiveParams(threadId)`
- All methods encoded via `JSONValue.encoded(params)` (line 276, 288, 324)

**Response decoding**:
- Raw `JSONValue` response decoded to `ThreadListResponseDTO`, `ThreadArchiveResponseDTO`, etc. via generic `decodeResponse(_, as:)` (line 821-829)
- `ThreadListResponseDTO` contains: `data` (array of `ThreadDTO`), `nextCursor`, `backwardsCursor`, `liveOverlay` (ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO)

---

### 7. SECRETS & HOST CONFIG CLIENT-SIDE

**Host configuration**:
- `DockHostConfiguration(endpoint: DockRelayEndpoint)` (DockHostConfiguration.swift:165-179)
- `DockRelayEndpoint(host: String, port: Int)` parsed from env var `CODEX_DOCK_HOSTS` (line 214) or hardcoded
- No validation of port against raw app-server port (4500) vs dock relay port (4510) (line 92-95)

**Secrets**:
- Optional `bearerToken` passed to `URLSessionWebSocketAppServerTransport` but not persisted (AppServerClient.swift:179-195)
- No token management in Dock client itself; assumes relay handles auth

**Local metadata**:
- Per-thread `LocalThreadMetadata` (rail color, custom label) stored locally via `FileLocalThreadMetadataStore` (DockStore.swift:596, 951-961)

---

### 8. CODEX COUPLING ASSESSMENT

**High coupling to Codex concepts:**
1. **ThreadSourceKind enum** with 9 hardcoded Codex-specific source types (exec, appServer, subAgent*)
2. **DockSessionScope** enum (.human, .agents) that maps to hardcoded query filters by origin type
3. **SessionStatus** enum reflecting Codex's thread state machine (notLoaded, active, idle, systemError, unknownOrigin)
4. **SessionOrigin** discriminated union with `SessionHumanOriginSubtype` (cli, vscode, customInteractive) and `SessionAgentOriginSubtype` (exec, appServer, subAgentReview, subAgentCompact, subAgentThreadSpawn, subAgentOther)
5. **Scope-level deduplication logic** (line 876-919) that implements Codex-specific conflict resolution (prefer human over agent, agent over unknown)
6. **liveOverlay merging** (line 164-172) that assumes relay returns per-scope health status
7. **Complex origin classification** (SessionSummaryMapper lines 227-277) that pattern-matches 30+ JSON keys to infer Codex source semantics

**What a provider-agnostic over-the-wire model would replace:**
- `ThreadSourceKind` → generic `sourceType: String` or namespace enum
- `SessionOriginKind/Subtype` → `originClassification: String` (no hardcoded subtypes)
- `DockSessionScope` → query parameter like `scope: String` (e.g., "human", "agents", "all")
- Deduplication preference logic → delegate to relay or remove (let relay return unique set)
- liveOverlay parsing → standardized health status object (e.g., `{ status: "healthy"/"degraded", reason?: String }`)
- ThreadStatusDTO active flags → generic `status: { type, metadata: JSONValue }`
- SessionSummaryText enum → simple `String | null`

---

### SUMMARY TABLE

| Layer | Coupling Level | Key Files | Codex-Specific Elements |
|-------|---|---|---|
| **Transport** | Low | AppServerClient.swift | WebSocket + JSON-RPC (generic) |
| **Protocol** | Medium | JSONRPC.swift, ThreadListDTO.swift | `ThreadSourceKind` enum, `ThreadStatusDTO`, `liveOverlay` |
| **Decoding** | High | SessionSummaryMapper.swift | Origin classification (30+ key patterns), hardcoded subtypes |
| **Merging** | High | DockStore.swift | `DockSessionScope`, conflict resolution (prefer human > agent) |
| **Failure Recovery** | Medium | AppServerClient.swift, DockStore.swift | Scope-level error tracking, partial snapshots, no stale-while-refresh |
| **Data Model** | High | SessionSummary.swift, DockRowViewModel | `SessionOrigin`, `SessionStatus`, origin evidence fields |
| **Refresh** | Low | DockStore.swift | `maxPages=1`, 5-second interval (constants, not logic) |

---

This architecture shows the client is **tightly bound to Codex's domain semantics**—particularly around source classification, scope bifurcation (human vs. agents), and multi-origin deduplication. A clean relay design would move all of that logic server-side and return a unified, provider-agnostic session list to the client.

- `refresh()` calls `reload(showLoading: false)` which re-fans to all hosts and scopes each time (line 531-532)
- Relies on AppServerClient's reconnect policy for connection recovery; no retry loop at Dock level

**AppServerClient reconnect policy** (AppServerClient.swift:615-650):
- `connectionPolicy: AppServerConnectionPolicy` can have optional `AppServerReconnectPolicy` (line 34-40)
- Reconnect loop runs with exponential backoff up to `maxAttempts` (line 634)
- Respects `foregroundWorkGate` to pause reconnects when backgrounded (line 638)
- Fires reconnect only if policy exists and `initializeParams` were set (line 627-630)

---

### 4. REFRESH MODEL & AUTO-REFRESH

**load() vs refresh()**:
- `load()` calls `reload(showLoading: true)` → shows `.loading` state (line 527-528)
- `refresh()` calls `reload(showLoading: false)` → updates in-place without loading indicator (line 531-532)

**Paging parameters**:
- `DockSessionQuery` hardcodes `maxPages: CodexDockConstants.Dock.activeSessionMaxPages = 1` for both human and agent scopes (line 19, 43, 49)
- Page limit (250 rows) applied per scope via `pageLimit(for:)` (line 160-162):
  - Agents: `CodexDockConstants.Dock.agentSessionPageLimit = 250`
  - Humans: `CodexDockConstants.Dock.humanSessionPageLimit = 250`
- No auto-refresh loop in DockStore; relies on external lifecycle coordinator to call `refresh()` periodically

**Auto-refresh interval**:
- `DockStore.defaultAutoRefreshInterval: Duration = .seconds(5)` (line 447, CodexDockConstants.Dock.autoRefreshInterval)
- Not used internally; must be invoked by view controller or lifecycle handler

---

### 5. CLIENT DATA MODEL

**SessionSummary** (Models/SessionSummary.swift:169-208):
- Fields: `id` (HostScopedThreadID), `backendSessionID`, `displayTitle`, `status` (SessionStatus), `repository` (SessionSummaryText), `workingDirectory`, `branch`, `lastActivity` (Date), `shortEventSummary`, `origin` (SessionOrigin)
- `SessionStatus`: `.unknown`, `.notLoaded`, `.idle`, `.systemError`, `.active(activeFlags)`
- `SessionOrigin`: wraps classified origin + evidence

**DockRowViewModel** (DockStore.swift:165-188):
- UI-facing projection: `id`, `backendSessionID`, `title`, `hostDisplayName`, `hostEndpoint`, `repository`, `branch`, `status` (DockRowStatusKind: running/idle/notLoaded/error/unknown), `lastActivity` (Date + relative text), `summary`, `rail` (color), `label`, `origin`
- Built by SessionRowProjector (State/SessionRowProjector.swift:3-127) which applies local metadata (rail, label) and formats timestamps

**DockSnapshot** (DockStore.swift:290-323):
- Contains: primary `host`, all `hosts`, `hostStates` (per-host load status), rows, scope load failures, scope conflicts, mapping failures, `isPartial` flag
- Immutable snapshot captures a moment in the merge

---

### 6. CLIENT-TO-RELAY COMMUNICATION

**Transport**: WebSocket over HTTP(S) (AppServerClient.swift:878-965):
- `URLSessionWebSocketAppServerTransport` wraps URLSessionWebSocketTask (line 886)
- URL constructed from `DockRelayEndpoint.webSocketURL` (DockHostConfiguration.swift:17-19): `ws://host:port/`
- Bearer token passed as "Authorization: Bearer ..." header if present (line 902-903)
- Maximum message size: `CodexDockConstants.AppServer.maximumMessageSize = 512 * 1024 * 1024` (line 13)

**JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol** (AppServer/JSONRPC.swift):
- Requests: `JSONRPCRequest(id, method, params)` encoded as JSON text (line 501-502)
- Responses: `JSONRPCResponse(id, result)` or `JSONRPCErrorObject(code, message)`
- Notifications: `JSONRPCNotification(method, params)` (no id)

**Method calls**:
- `thread/list` (AppServerClient.swift:270-280): params = `ThreadListParams` (cursor, limit, sortKey, sortDirection, modelProviders=[], sourceKinds, archived)
- `thread/archive`, `thread/unarchive` (line 318-340): params = `ThreadArchiveParams(threadId)`
- All methods encoded via `JSONValue.encoded(params)` (line 276, 288, 324)

**Response decoding**:
- Raw `JSONValue` response decoded to `ThreadListResponseDTO`, `ThreadArchiveResponseDTO`, etc. via generic `decodeResponse(_, as:)` (line 821-829)
- `ThreadListResponseDTO` contains: `data` (array of `ThreadDTO`), `nextCursor`, `backwardsCursor`, `liveOverlay` (ThreadListLiveOverlayDTO)

---

### 7. SECRETS & HOST CONFIG CLIENT-SIDE

**Host configuration**:
- `DockHostConfiguration(endpoint: DockRelayEndpoint)` (DockHostConfiguration.swift:165-179)
- `DockRelayEndpoint(host: String, port: Int)` parsed from env var `CODEX_DOCK_HOSTS` (line 214) or hardcoded
- No validation of port against raw app-server port (4500) vs dock relay port (4510) (line 92-95)

**Secrets**:
- Optional `bearerToken` passed to `URLSessionWebSocketAppServerTransport` but not persisted (AppServerClient.swift:179-195)
- No token management in Dock client itself; assumes relay handles auth

**Local metadata**:
- Per-thread `LocalThreadMetadata` (rail color, custom label) stored locally via `FileLocalThreadMetadataStore` (DockStore.swift:596, 951-961)

---

### 8. CODEX COUPLING ASSESSMENT

**High coupling to Codex concepts:**
1. **ThreadSourceKind enum** with 9 hardcoded Codex-specific source types (exec, appServer, subAgent*)
2. **DockSessionScope** enum (.human, .agents) that maps to hardcoded query filters by origin type
3. **SessionStatus** enum reflecting Codex's thread state machine (notLoaded, active, idle, systemError, unknownOrigin)
4. **SessionOrigin** discriminated union with `SessionHumanOriginSubtype` (cli, vscode, customInteractive) and `SessionAgentOriginSubtype` (exec, appServer, subAgentReview, subAgentCompact, subAgentThreadSpawn, subAgentOther)
5. **Scope-level deduplication logic** (line 876-919) that implements Codex-specific conflict resolution (prefer human over agent, agent over unknown)
6. **liveOverlay merging** (line 164-172) that assumes relay returns per-scope health status
7. **Complex origin classification** (SessionSummaryMapper lines 227-277) that pattern-matches 30+ JSON keys to infer Codex source semantics

**What a provider-agnostic over-the-wire model would replace:**
- `ThreadSourceKind` → generic `sourceType: String` or namespace enum
- `SessionOriginKind/Subtype` → `originClassification: String` (no hardcoded subtypes)
- `DockSessionScope` → query parameter like `scope: String` (e.g., "human", "agents", "all")
- Deduplication preference logic → delegate to relay or remove (let relay return unique set)
- liveOverlay parsing → standardized health status object (e.g., `{ status: "healthy"/"degraded", reason?: String }`)
- ThreadStatusDTO active flags → generic `status: { type, metadata: JSONValue }`
- SessionSummaryText enum → simple `String | null`

---

### SUMMARY TABLE

| Layer | Coupling Level | Key Files | Codex-Specific Elements |
|-------|---|---|---|
| **Transport** | Low | AppServerClient.swift | WebSocket + JSON-RPC (generic) |
| **Protocol** | Medium | JSONRPC.swift, ThreadListDTO.swift | `ThreadSourceKind` enum, `ThreadStatusDTO`, `liveOverlay` |
| **Decoding** | High | SessionSummaryMapper.swift | Origin classification (30+ key patterns), hardcoded subtypes |
| **Merging** | High | DockStore.swift | `DockSessionScope`, conflict resolution (prefer human > agent) |
| **Failure Recovery** | Medium | AppServerClient.swift, DockStore.swift | Scope-level error tracking, partial snapshots, no stale-while-refresh |
| **Data Model** | High | SessionSummary.swift, DockRowViewModel | `SessionOrigin`, `SessionStatus`, origin evidence fields |
| **Refresh** | Low | DockStore.swift | `maxPages=1`, 5-second interval (constants, not logic) |

---

This architecture shows the client is **tightly bound to Codex's domain semantics**—particularly around source classification, scope bifurcation (human vs. agents), and multi-origin deduplication. A clean relay design would move all of that logic server-side and return a unified, provider-agnostic session list to the client.
